title: 'Home Improvement' star says Patricia Richardson got 'tired' of fighting for sitcom
summary: Taran Noah Smith reveals Patricia Richardson fought to keep "Home Improvement" realistic as new writers pushed scripts in a different direction.
story: Patricia Richardson explained to Fox News Digital that Tim Allen was better on "Home Improvement" than many of the seasoned actors she had worked with before.
"Home Improvement" star Taran Noah Smith is shedding new light on why the hit 1990s sitcom came to an end.

The 42-year-old former actor was seven-years-old when he landed the role of Mark Taylor, the youngest son of Tim "The Tool Man" Taylor (Tim Allen) and his wife Jill Taylor (Patricia Richardson) in 1991.

The sitcom, which was based on Allen's stand-up comedy persona, centered on Tim, a television host known for his home improvement show, "Tool Time," and his family life with Jill, Mark and older sons Brad (Zachery Ty Bryan) and Randy (Jonathan Taylor Thomas).
"Home Improvement" star Taran Noah Smith opened up about why the hit sitcom came to an end. (Patricia Richardson Instagram/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
'HOME IMPROVEMENT' STAR JONATHAN TAYLOR THOMAS ARRESTED FOR ALLEGED PUBLIC INTOXICATION, RESISTING DEPUTY

"Home Improvement" became one of the highest-rated shows of the '90s and ran for eight seasons and aired 204 episodes. However, the show concluded in 1999 after Richardson declined to return for a proposed ninth season.

During a recent appearance on Tom Scharpling and Julia Vickerman's podcast "Outgrown" podcast, Smith reflected on his time starring on the show and weighed in on the reasons behind Richardson's departure.
TIM ALLEN SAYS HE 'NEVER REALLY WANTED' TO BE A DAD AND OPENS UP ABOUT SOBRIETY AND FATHERHOOD REGRETS
Smith recalled that Richardson joined the cast as Jill just days before the pilot was taped after producers replaced Frances Fisher, the actress originally cast as Tim's wife, during rehearsals.
"Home Improvement" was one of the highes-rated shows of the 1990s and ran for eight seasons from 1991 to 1998.  (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

"When they brought Patricia in, there was just a much better chemistry," he said. "And she had her own kid. She had just given birth to twins, and she had one older kid who was about my age. She really brought a lot more of a realistic mom energy to her, and she fought throughout the whole show to keep the show more realistic."
"She would tell the writers, ‘A mother would never say this,’ and get them to change it," he added.
Smith said he "definitely" agreed with Richardson's input though he acknowledged that he and the show's other child stars weren't really involved in conversations about the script.
"They'd do a run-through of the script on Monday and then the kids would go to school usually, and they would continue to discuss the script," he said.
Smith recalled that there were creative disagreements on set after a new creative team replaced the show's original writers and producers.
ROSEANNE BARR HASN’T SPOKEN TO TV SISTER LAURIE METCALF SINCE SHOW’S CANCELLATION

The show followed TV host Tim "The Tool Man" Taylor (Tim Allen) and his family life with wife Jill Taylor (Patricia Richardson) and sons Brad (Zachery Ty Bryan), Randy (Jonathan Taylor Thomas) and Mark (Taran Noah Smith).  (Getty)

"The original creators only did the first couple seasons, and then they moved on, and they brought in a whole other group of writer/producers," he remembered. "Those guys, very few of them had kids, and the show kind of started to go in a different direction, at least the scripts we'd get on Monday."

"It was really Pat, the mom, who fought the good fight to make it more realistic because oftentimes it would just be something that was very out of character just to sell a joke, just to set up a joke," he continued. "It's like, ‘Wait, this is not what the characters are about.’"
ROSEANNE BARR CALLS FORMER CO-STAR A 'BRAINWASHED BIGOT' AFTER HE SAID REBOOT WAS 'RIGHTFULLY CANCELED'

Smith speculated that Allen was reluctant to appear overly controlling after witnessing what happened on another sitcom, "Roseanne." "Roseanne," which became an instant hit after it premiered in 1988, was created by "Home Improvement" co-creator Matt Williams. Like "Home Improvement," Roseanne was built around its star's stand-up comedy voice and persona.

However, Barr clashed behind-the-scenes with producers and writers, including Williams, over the direction and tone of the show. The tensions between the two led to Williams leaving after the first season. Barr later gained more influence and was credited as a creator in later seasons.
Patricia Richardson starred opposite Tim Allen in "Home Improvement," but would not be interested in doing a reboot. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
‘THE OFFICE’ STAR JENNA FISCHER EXPOSES THE GRUELING REALITY THAT FORCED HER OFF TV

"I think Tim was overall maybe a bit worried about being a tyrant because the same creators created ‘Roseanne,’ and Roseanne took over the show and fired the creators, fired everybody," Smith recalled. "Actually, all our camera crew had been fired in one day from ‘Roseanne’ and came over to us. So, Tim was always, I think, more hands-off with that, not wanting to be tyrannical, which meant that it was a lot more on Pat to push."
"That's one of the reasons why the show ended up eventually ending, because she was just tired of it, of having to fight to make it realistic all the time," he continued.
JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS

"And Tim was getting far more money than she was," Smith added. "That was her actual way of stopping. She said she'd do a ninth season if she got paid the same amount as Tim, knowing they wouldn't do it."
Smith's recollection of why Richardson left "Home Improvement" echoes what the actress has said for years about her experience on the show and the reasons for her departure.
During a May 2024 interview with the Los Angeles Times, Richardson recalled that the creators emphasized the importance of the character of Jill and her relationship with Tim.

Smith said that Allen took a more "hands-off" approach to creative disagreements with directors and writers, leaving Richardson to fight for character consistency.  ( ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
"When I took the job, they said it wasn’t meant to be the Tim Allen show. It was meant to be our show," she said. "I’ve always said, I don’t want to play the thankless wife."

Richardson recalled having creative disagreements with male writers over how Jill would react to specific situations, remembering one instance in which she was told, "Pat, it’s not like we don’t understand women. We’re married to them."
The actress, who earned four Primetime Emmy Award nominations for her performance as Jill, told the LA Times that she made the decision to leave the show.

Richardson told the LA Times she decided during the eighth season that it would be her last, citing a desire to spend more time with her children after her divorce and her belief that the sitcom had run its course, pointing to Jonathan Taylor Thomas' departure and declining ratings.

Smith said that Richardson left the show after growing "tired" of fighting to make the show realistic.  (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

The actress also felt that Disney failed to recognize her creative contributions to the series, saying she helped shape her character and storylines but was denied a producer credit, even as Allen became an executive producer.
"I told everybody, there’s not enough money in the world to get me to do a ninth year. This show is over. It needs to end," Richardson recalled.

Richardson recalled that ABC unexpectedly offered to continue the show with a 25-episode ninth season. She said the network's parent company, Disney, proposed paying her a salary of $1 million an episode, while Allen would be paid $2 million an episode.

Though she recalled Allen immediately accepting the offer, she said she countered with terms that she knew the studio would reject. Richardson told the outlet that she requested equal pay with Allen and an executive producer credit.

"I knew that Disney would in no way pay me that much. That was my way to say ‘no’ and was a little bit of a flip-off to Disney," Richardson said. "I’d been there all this time, and they never even paid me a third of what Tim was making, and I was working my a-- off. I was a big reason why women were watching."

title: Bruce Campbell says Hollywood studios left ‘very sour’ taste after he was 'kicked out' of lead role
summary: After a cancer diagnosis and decades in Hollywood, Bruce Campbell and wife Ida Gearon filmed "Ernie & Emma" entirely in their home state of Oregon.
story: "Ernie & Emma" actor Bruce Campbell tells Fox News Digital why studio films left him with a bad taste.
Bruce Campbell is taking a chainsaw to the Hollywood playbook.

The "Evil Dead" star is ditching the traditional studio system for "Ernie & Emma," his new independent film that puts him firmly in the driver's seat after decades of navigating Hollywood — and after one early studio experience left a bad taste.

"The first studio film I ever did, I got kicked out of the lead," Campbell told Fox News Digital. "The movie was re-edited, retitled and never came out. So, the taste in my mouth from studios is very sour."
KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE
Actor Bruce Campbell wrote, directed and produced "Ernie & Emma." ("Ernie & Emma")
That experience stuck with the cult-favorite actor, who said he has long wanted to make a project without studio executives calling the shots.
"It was time to be unbridled in my life," Campbell said.
WATCH: BRUCE CAMPBELL SAYS HOLLYWOOD STUDIOS LEFT 'VERY SOUR' TASTE IN HIS MOUTH
The decision carries extra weight following Campbell's cancer diagnosis, which he disclosed in March.
Campbell said earlier this month on "The Adam Carolla Show" podcast that doctors had given him an estimated five years to live, but he remains focused on treatment and continuing his work.
The actor wrote, directed, produced and stars in "Ernie & Emma," which he made independently with his wife and longtime partner, Ida Gearon.
For Campbell, the project represents a return to the kind of creative freedom he experienced early in his career with "The Evil Dead."
Bruce Campbell plays Ernie. ("Ernie & Emma")
TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS
"The very first movie we did, ‘Evil Dead,’ was the only other movie I've ever done free and clear of the studio system," he said. "So, I liked the taste of it early on."
"I wanted to do something like this for a long time, and my wife finally said, ‘Quit talking about it. Let's do it. Let's pull the trigger. Let's make this movie," he recalled.
WATCH: ACTOR BRUCE CAMPBELL TOUTS MAKING FILM WITH WIFE: 'WE NEVER ARGUED ONCE'
'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD AFTER YEARS OF REJECTION AND ‘ABUSE’
The actor has little interest in pretending creative control is easy to maintain when someone else is financing the production.

"Creative freedom is absolutely everything," Campbell said. "If you consider yourself an artiste, or you're in the arts, the only way that artists have to deal with people, outside of themselves, is to go look for money."
Bruce Campbell appears during a memorial scene in "Ernie & Emma." ("Ernie & Emma")
"Ernie & Emma" marks a dramatic departure from the horror and action roles that made Campbell a genre icon.
The movie follows Ernie Tyler, a small-town pear salesman who embarks on a road trip through Pear Valley, Oregon, after his beloved wife, Emma, dies.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Emma leaves Ernie a detailed list of instructions for scattering her ashes, sending him on a journey through grief, love and the possibility of starting over.
Campbell and Gearon filmed the movie entirely in southern Oregon, turning their home state into the backdrop for the story — and their own lives into an unconventional production setup.
Gearon, a longtime costume designer, encouraged Campbell to keep the shoot close to home.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"She goes, ‘Bruce, we should shoot in Oregon. You should sleep in your own bed. You should [be having lunch] at the house,’" Campbell said. "And so, I did, and it was a very bizarre experience, but I'll never go back now."
Bruce Campbell said his wife encouraged him to shoot the movie close to home. ("Ernie & Emma")
"Best part of working with my wife was that, for once, we didn't argue," he said. "We argue a lot and when we made the movie we never argued once because we had a singular goal, singular vision."
After more than three decades together, Campbell said his relationship with Gearon has evolved into something deeper than romance.
"Boy, my wife, she is rock solid. She's a good human being from A to Z. I trust her," he said.

"The other day we said to each other, we've been together so long we're actually family now."

title: Hugh Hefner's 'most sexy' Playboy model reveals how Anna Nicole Smith changed her life
summary: Sandra Taylor shares stories of dating Fabio, shooting romance novel covers and Dan Aykroyd buying her SAG card after her Playboy career launched.
story: Sandra Taylor reveals how her friendship with Anna Nicole Smith unexpectedly helped launch her Playboy career and recalls the star’s sweeter side.
Anna Nicole Smith unknowingly transformed the life of the woman Hugh Hefner once called his "most sexy model."

Sandra Taylor, who made hearts race as a Playboy cover girl during the '90s, is now the head sommelier at Allegiant Stadium, home of the Las Vegas Raiders. But long before then, her friendship with the 1993 Playmate of the Year changed the course of her life.
Taylor recently appeared on Sports Illustrated Swimsuit model Kim Alexis' podcast, "Unexpired," where she reflected on her life and career.
LARRY BIRKHEAD CELEBRATES DAUGHTER DANNIELYNN'S 20TH BIRTHDAY WITH RARE PHOTOS
Sandra Taylor attends the "Raising Helen" Los Angeles premiere arrivals at El Capitan Theatre in Hollywood, California. (WireImage)

"I was friends with Anna Nicole Smith, and she was such a darling," Taylor recalled to Fox News Digital. "We shared two makeup artists. One was in New York, one was in LA. And they introduced us very, very early on to her coming here from Texas, and we became friends. She needed a place to stay when she first came out here."
Anna Nicole Smith in a publicity portrait for the movie "Naked Gun 33 1/3: The Final Insult," 1994. (Getty Images)

A visit to Smith on the set of "Naked Gun 33 1/3: The Final Insult" changed the course of Taylor's career. After Smith's makeup artist urged her to meet with Playboy during its 40th anniversary search, Smith encouraged her friend to go for it. The opportunity led Taylor to Playboy and launched a new chapter in her life.
WATCH: SANDRA TAYLOR REVEALS HOW ANNA NICOLE SMITH LED HER TO PLAYBOY
"It was my friendship with Anna Nicole Smith ... it led me right there," said Taylor.
Model Sandra Taylor attends the Playboy Magazine party honoring her on June 8, 1995, at Gauguin at the Plaza in New York City. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

"I never, in a million years growing up, thought I would ever be in Playboy," she said. "It just seemed so out of the realm of reality. I was full speed ahead to be a mathematician just like my dad. ... I studied macroeconomics, microeconomics, statistics, differential equations, and I was a dream dancer."
Actor Sandra Taylor arrives at the National Lampoon premiere of "One, Two, Many" at the Arclight Theatre on April 10, 2008, in Los Angeles. (Getty Images)

"I was only 19 years old when my dad passed away," she continued. "It was on my college campus at SUNY Purchase. He was walking with my mom, and he had a heart attack just out of the blue and passed away. And then I never went back to that campus again. Books in locker; never went back. Never looked back. I always used to joke, 'I wonder if my books are still in my locker,' because I never cleared it out. But after that, when he passed away, the math died along with him, and I just didn't want to do it anymore."
Actress Sandra Taylor appeared on "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno" on Aug. 30, 1995. (NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)

After her father's sudden death, Taylor abandoned her plans to pursue math and embraced a career in modeling. Looking back, she remains grateful for her friendship with Smith, whom she credits with helping open the door to Playboy before Smith died in 2007 at 39.

"I remember how sweet she was," said Taylor. "She was really, really a sweet girl and loved her son so much. She really wanted to be a great mom. She was really a sweetheart, just a really nice girl. I don't think she could hurt a fly."
Anna Nicole Smith appears with her son Daniel on the Harald-Schmidt Show on June 24, 1997, in Germany. (Frank Hempel/United Archives via Getty Images)
For Taylor, posing for Playboy was only the beginning. She said it led to a friendship with Hefner that lasted until his death in 2017 at 91.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Sandra Taylor is seen here with Playboy founder Hugh Hefner. (Courtesy of Sandra Taylor)

"Even when you do the magazine, it doesn't end there," Taylor explained. "Hef opens up his home for years to come. ... Because I was good friends with Kimberley, his wife, I was able to fly on their jet. I was able to really experience him as a family man, and how kind he was, too. I loved his laugh. If I look back, his laugh to me was the most infectious, wonderful thing about him. And I miss him. I really think he changed the trajectory of things for me. I'm sure it closed some doors ... but I wouldn't change it for the world."
Sandra Taylor told Fox News Digital she had a lasting friendship with Hugh Hefner. (Courtesy of Sandra Taylor)
Decades later, Taylor said she learned what Hefner thought of her Playboy photos.
Sandra Taylor is seen here on the cover of the July 1995 issue of Playboy magazine. (Alamy)

"You know Traci Bingham from 'Baywatch?'" said Taylor. "She had told me when she went in to discuss doing Playboy, it was right around the time my layout was [going] to press. She goes, 'I want to do a layout just like that! Who's that?' And he was like, 'Oh, this is Sandra Taylor. She's our most sexy model we've ever had.' I go, 'Why did you wait all these years to tell me that amazing piece of trivia? I would've loved to have known years ago what Hef thought about me.'"
Traci Bingham from Seasons 7 and 8 of "Baywatch," which aired from 1989 to 2001. (Courtesy Everett Collection)

"I always knew he was so into blondes, like real blondes," said Taylor. "So to think he was a fan of my photos as well. I just thought he had to use diversity in the magazine. Brunettes, blondes ... every single walk of life you want to represent in the magazine. But I always thought he favored blondes. So, when she told me that, it was so beautiful. ... I was like, 'Traci, could you tell me that one more time?'"
Hugh Hefner and actress Tracy Bingham pose for a photo outside the Barfly on Aug. 17, 2002, in Hollywood. (Getty Images)
Becoming a sought-after model had plenty of perks for Taylor — like catching Fabio’s eye.
WATCH: SANDRA TAYLOR RECALLS DATING FABIO, POSING FOR ROMANCE COVERS

"Shooting the romance covers with Fabio was exactly what you would imagine it would be," said Taylor. "These elaborate wardrobes — the fan, the hair, everything. It was so wonderful. It was in New York. I met Fabio at this gym called the Vertical Club. He was so sweet. We dated a few times, and he was lovely. He said, 'Have you ever thought about doing a romance novel cover?' And I was like, 'No, but I would love to.'"
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Italian actor and fashion model Fabio Lanzoni poses for a portrait with Brenda Joyce's book "Scandalous Love" in New York, on Nov. 8, 1992. (Getty Images)

"I was on the yes train from the get-go," said Taylor. "I always was interested. I always had an open mind, and I always kept myself very interested in anything that came my way. ... I don't know how many romance novel covers we did together, but it was a lot. You shoot many, many in one [day]. So that was really fun. That was a great experience."
As an actress, Taylor frequently worked with director Garry Marshall. She also appeared in projects with Steven Seagal, Robert De Niro and other Hollywood stars.
From left: Victoria Silvstedt, Carmen Electra, Sandra Taylor and Miss March Tina Jordan pose together at an event, date unknown. (WireImage)

"Steven Seagal was really kind to me," said Taylor. "He was a real gentleman to me. Every time I went to audition, and it was multiple times, there were more beautiful women. The rooms were just packed with beautiful women. I just braced myself. But he was so professional. I remember I wore my lucky pink Chanel suit. The first thing he said to me was, 'Oh, my wife has a suit similar to that.' He was just so chivalrous and kind to me."
Canadian comedian and actor Dan Aykroyd with Playmate Sandra Taylor, circa 1992. (Getty Images)

"And Dan Aykroyd, I remember he was incredibly generous too. He bought me my SAG card for my first movie. Dan was like, 'I would love to pay for that for you and one day be able to say that I bought you your SAG card.' That was a beautiful surprise. He was also very kind and welcoming. I'll never forget that."

Sandra Taylor is the head sommelier for the Las Vegas Raiders. (Courtesy of Sandra Taylor.)

Taylor's life today is "a little different," she said. She lost her home of 24 years in the 2025 Palisades Fire. She continues to rebuild and has embraced a new role as a professional sommelier. She also helped create Raider Rosé.
Sandra Taylor is seen here holding a bottle of her rosé. (Courtesy of Sandra Taylor)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Today, Sandra Taylor is embracing the next chapter of her life. (Courtesy of Sandra Taylor)
"I'm proud of the life I've led," said Taylor. "I've faced ups and downs, but I've been blessed. And I'm always ready for what life throws at me."

title: Child actor recalls receiving disturbing prison mail from fans during peak of '90s fame
summary: Justin Cooper reveals his mother shielded him from disturbing prison mail he received as a child star of the 1997 hit comedy "Liar Liar."
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Justin Cooper was eight years old when he began experiencing the not-so-friendly side of fame.

story: Sylvester Stallone told Fox News Digital he is still happy with his choice to permanently relocate to Florida from Hollywood last year.
Sylvester Stallone isn't looking for pity.

The action star opened up about a childhood marked by abandonment, violence and an almost total absence of affection in a new interview, telling The New York Times he deliberately left some of the darkest stories out of his book because he didn't want readers to feel sorry for him.
"I didn't put a lot of stuff in the book because I didn't want a pity party … but it was insane," he admitted.

After his parent’s divorce, Stallone spent time living with his father in Maryland. He described his father as volatile and physically abusive.
"The next thing you know — wham! He had very big hands. You just learned to duck a little bit."
One memory particularly stayed with Stallone.
The Hollywood star said his father sent him to a store before church to buy bread. He returned with nut bread after running into friends.
"And he kicked me in the stomach and hit me and like laid me out, got in the car, and went to church."
Stallone said he was left lying in the street, saying, "Really, it's unbelievable. It's unbelievable."

Years later, Stallone confronted his father. When he was in his 40s, Stallone told him, "I wish you and I could be the same age for three minutes." When his father asked him why, he said, "Because I'd like to give you some of your own medicine, and you would know what it'd be like to have your a-- kicked."

The "Rocky" star connected that fierceness to one of the characters he's best known for.
"So, when people go, ‘Where do you get the ferocity to play Rambo?' Genetic," he said.
Stallone additionally recalled that his mother never showed affection toward him.
SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!'
"My mother never — and my brother will attest — hugged me. Ever, ever," Stallone shared.

His father rarely showed affection either. But when Stallone was about 9, he said he fell asleep in the car after working around his father's horses. His father placed Stallone's head on his knee and rested his hand on his head.
"And I never got over that," he admitted.

Earlier in the interview, Stallone described being sent to live in a boarding house when he was very young, where his parents visited only once a month.

"I just was raised by strangers, you know, in a boarding house. And it became sort of a natural environment. And my parents were really never nurturing, so this was actually a bonus compared to where I was living."
That emotional deprivation, Stallone acknowledged, shaped the man he became.
When asked whether it made him tough, he replied, "In the wrong way, yeah, it did. It made me very tough."

But the toughness came at a cost. Stallone said he didn't experience what he considers "real, real, real, real true love" until he was around 70, when he experienced it with his wife and kids, saying, "And that's a big pity. It really is."

title: 'Mike & Molly' star Billy Gardell reveals weight loss surgery 'probably saved' his life
summary: Billy Gardell says bariatric surgery "probably saved my life" after type 2 diabetes and heart concerns forced him to make a drastic decision.
story: Ethan Suplee reflects on the ongoing responsibility that comes with becoming a public weight loss success story and explains why consistent support from like-minded people keeps him on track.
"Mike & Molly" star Billy Gardell is sharing how his dramatic weight loss after bariatric surgery in 2021 changed his life.

During a recent appearance on the "Breaking Bread" podcast, the 57-year-old actor said his decision to undergo the surgery "probably saved my life" and described the circumstances that led to him deciding that was the right route for him.
He explained that he had developed Type 2 diabetes and "some cholesterol stuff, some heart stuff," joking that his doctor told him that, "after 50, the warranties start running out."

"You can't outrun those. I think the only reason I was able to survive as long as I did is one, I got decent genetics, and two was I played some sports when I was younger. So, I was a big fat guy, but I was a pretty solid fat guy, and I could carry the weight for a long time, but eventually you can't outrun that."
Gardell credits his weight loss surgery for saving his life. (Getty Images)
'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS ONE HARD TRUTH FUELED HIS 300-POUND WEIGHT LOSS
After a certain point, Gardell said, his doctor approached him and said, "You have to do something."

"I got to the point where I hurt my knee, and I couldn't even walk for exercise, and I was like, I have to do something drastic," he said. "So, I got the surgery, and it's been a couple years now, and I probably saved my life. I'm not on any medication. Diabetes is gone."

Five years after the surgery, the actor explained, he has "to be real selective" about what he eats because he only has "12 ounces to work with," but he said the issue with that is "the fat Hulk is still running around" in his mind wanting to overindulge.

Aside from saving his life, the surgery and resulting weight loss also allowed him to do things he couldn't do before, including hiking with his wife and buying something "off the rack" when shopping at the mall.
Gardell is enjoying the little things in life since losing weight. (Michael Simon/Getty Images)

"It's just those little freedoms that you go, 'Wow, man. I'm so grateful I can do this now,'" he said. "I know those are simple, stupid things, but they mean the world to me."
Gardell explained he decided to get healthy not only for himself, but also for his wife, Patty Knight and their son, William, calling them "my motivating factors."

"It was like I don't want to survive what I've survived, succeed where I succeeded and then not be able to get out of a chair. So, I had to look that in its face. And for anybody out there struggling, if I can do it, you can do it. And don't let nobody tell you different. Do whatever it takes."
Throughout his life, Gardell said he would often fluctuate, losing and gaining 30 pounds every year, noting that, at his heaviest, he weighed 379 pounds.

title: Princess Diana considered becoming first lady after American politician courted her, brother claims
summary: Princess Diana’s brother reveals surprising details about her private life, including a powerful American suitor, royal tensions and plans for a fresh start.
story: A reported movie about Princess Diana spearheaded by Prince Harry for the 30th anniversary of her death is causing royal family tension. Johnny Joey Jones reacts with a theory about Markle acting as an American plant to dismantle the monarchy, sparking laughs from the co-hosts.
Princess Diana’s younger brother, Charles Spencer, released his memoir "Swan Song," about the beloved royal this week, revealing new details about the late royal’s life behind palace walls.
From claims about then-Prince Charles’ treatment of Diana to an American politician who reportedly courted her after her divorce, here are some of the memoir’s biggest revelations.
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"Swan Song" is out now. (Steinway)
Spencer wrote that on the morning Diana died, Prince Charles sounded "giddily elated — like a lottery winner," he remembered thinking at the time.
He wrote that Charles was "strangely matter-of-fact, given the enormity of the disaster."
PRINCESS DIANA'S HONEYMOON LETTER REVEALS A YOUNG BRIDE 'PLAYING WITH GROWN-UPS' IN THE ROYAL FAMILY
Charles Spencer wrote a memoir about his sister, Princess Diana, called "Swan Song." (The Spencer Family; Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)
In hindsight, Spencer wrote, he believed that Charles’ first reaction to her death was that it likely freed him up to "marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not."
He also wrote that while they were arguing over funeral arrangements, Charles told him, "Rest assured … we'll forget her soon enough!"
PRINCE HARRY'S RUMORED DIANA FILM 'MIGHT FEEL LIKE ANOTHER BETRAYAL' TO PRINCE WILLIAM AS RIFT GROWS: EXPERT
Spencer said he was stunned for a few seconds before responding, "I can’t believe you just said that," before hanging up.

Earlier in their conversation, Spencer wrote that Charles accused the Spencer family of having no sense of duty because Spencer had objected to Princes Harry and William walking behind their mother’s coffin.
Princess Diana and Charles Spencer smiling together as kids (Central Press/Getty Images)
PRINCESS DIANA NEVER FORGAVE SARAH FERGUSON FOR ONE BETRAYAL THAT ENDED THEIR FRIENDSHIP: BOOK
Spencer wrote that he believed the diatribe was the result of Charles’ "pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death."
After the excerpt from the book was released last week, Buckingham Palace issued a rare statement.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said.
Prince Charles and Princess Diana ride in a carriage on their wedding day. (WireImage)
PRINCESS DIANA COULD HAVE SURVIVED FATAL PARIS CRASH IF SHE MADE ONE SIMPLE CHOICE, INVESTIGATOR SAYS

Spencer wrote that, after falling in love with heart surgeon Dr. Hasnat Khan after her divorce, Diana had the "naïve yet impossible" dream of moving to South Africa — where Spencer lived at the time — with her boyfriend because England had become "intolerable" to her.
"Might they, she dared hope, move there together, and carve out a life?" he wrote.
He said she dreamed that Khan could work at a hospital in Cape Town, and they could live "happily — normally" near her brother.
"The other side of the world seemed to offer the possibility of asylum," he wrote.
INSIDE PRINCESS DIANA AND JFK JR.'S SECRET MEETING THAT FUELED ROMANCE RUMORS FOR DECADES

Spencer said that Diana once asked him if he thought she’d make a good American first lady, explaining that one of her "many powerful aging American suitors, keen to secure her as the ultimate trophy wife, had told her he was sure to win the presidency if she married him."
Princess Diana and Prince Charles in 1991 (Getty Images)
He said that Diana was more "titillated" by the idea of living in the White House than by the prospect of marrying the "would-be elderly husband."

Diana, he said, had a "mischievous attraction to reinventing herself in a role that would make her enemies in the British Royal Family sick with jealousy, while ushering in an era of glamour in the White House that would surely have surpassed even that of the Jackie Kennedy years."

Despite "Panorama" reporter Martin Bashir allegedly telling Diana a series of falsehoods, including that she was being surveilled by MI6, that Prince William was unwittingly bugging her through a device on his watch and that her children’s nanny had aborted Prince Charles' child after an affair, Diana almost canceled the interview, Spencer said.

He wrote that the princess pulled out a few days before the interview was scheduled to take place.

But Bashir and the show’s executive producer persisted, Spencer wrote. He said they arranged a clandestine meeting in a parking garage, where Spencer believes they persuaded Diana that her life was in "imminent" danger and that doing the interview was the best way to protect herself.
Spencer's handwritten eulogy notes for Diana's funeral (The Spencer Family)
Spencer said he had a conversation with Charles after his own father’s funeral, during which Charles told him he was "lucky" his father had died because he got to inherit when he was "so young."

Charles allegedly said that while Spencer was inheriting his ancestral home of Althorp in his 20s, the prince complained that he was 43 and employed 50 people, "but my parents insist on treating me like — like a child!"

He also wrote that when a senior courtier told Queen Elizabeth that Charles resented a reprimand she had delivered through the courtier, the queen dismissed the concern, telling him, "He even resented it when I taught him the alphabet."

Spencer also wrote that Diana told him early in her relationship with the prince that the queen had once considered having Charles’ ears pinned back because their "protrusion" had caused him to be teased at school and mocked by the media. Prince Philip put a stop to it, however, according to Spencer.
Spencer added that he didn’t know whether the story was true, but Diana believed it.
Earl Charles Spencer's book "Swan Song" was released this week. (Getty Images)

Later in the book, Spencer wrote that when Diana first told him she planned to divorce Charles, she claimed that the prince was "in love with his valet."
Spencer said he found the claim improbable but didn't press her for more information because he was focused on the realization that she was ending her marriage and her "dreams."
Princess Diana sits on the steps of Highgrove House.  (Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

Spencer wrote that his sister had "traditionally feminine" interests, which included collecting numerous stuffed animals as a child. She loved flowers, especially forget-me-nots, listened to the Beatles and David Bowie and liked the soap opera "Crossroads."
As she got older, Spencer wrote, she "devoured" romance novels by Barbara Cartland, whom he said mainly wrote about aristocratic men pursuing virginal women and eventually living happily ever after.

She also once told Spencer that she had watched the equally romantic "The Sound of Music" 16 times.
Spencer's book was released nearly a year before the 30th anniversary of Diana's death. Diana was killed in a car crash in Paris Aug. 31, 1997.
Buckingham Palace told Fox News Digital, "We won’t be offering any further comment."

title: Brandi Glanville emptied her 401(k) after spending ‘hundreds of thousands’ on medical bills
summary: Brandi Glanville suffered a concussion, perforated eardrum and cracked rib on "Special Forces" after a helicopter water jump went terribly wrong.
story: Reality star Brandi Glanville explains why her recent financial strain made turning down opportunities more difficult and pushed her to prove she could perform again on FOX's "Special Forces."
Brandi Glanville needed a comeback — personally and financially.
After years of costly health struggles turned her life upside down, the former "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star told Fox News Digital she needed to get back to work.

"I had the leisure of saying no in the past, but then I had all these medical bills and whatnot," she admitted. "So I had to say yes. And it was kind of like at a time where I needed to prove to myself that I could do it again."
BRANDI GLANVILLE ENDS UP IN URGENT CARE AFTER TRYING VIRAL TIKTOK TREND

Brandi Glanville revealed that she emptied her 401(k) and spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on medical bills while searching for answers to her debilitating health problems.  (FOX via Getty Images)
But for Glanville, the financial fallout from her health battle has been just as daunting as the physical toll.

"The medical system here is broken," Glanville explained. "So I have, like, from 8 a.m. on, I have creditors from, like, medical things calling me, like from Cedars-Sinai. It's out of control. Like I spent hundreds of thousands of dollars that I had saved. I emptied my 401(k). And it's all for medical bills. And I had insurance, and they told me nothing was wrong. I'm so angry. You know, going into my mid-fifties I had a cushion and that's gone. So it's very scary right now."

After years of suffering, Glanville revealed in September that she had been diagnosed with highly resistant ESBL Klebsiella and Enterobacter with biofilm, coccidioidomycosis, also known as Valley fever, Demodex dermatitis and mononucleosis.
Glanville has said her daily IV treatment was expected to cost between $3,300 and $6,000 per month.

Glanville previously shared that she believed she picked up a parasite after visiting Morocco in 2023. She suffered from facial paralysis and was initially diagnosed with stress-induced angioedema. She told Fox News Digital at the time that she spent more than $70,000 in an attempt to find an answer to the medical mystery that consumed her daily life and disfigured her face.
After everything her body had already endured, Glanville was determined to test her limits on "Special Forces: World's Toughest Test." One challenge pushed those limits further than she expected.

While filming the show, Glanville said contestants were trained on how to fall from a helicopter into the water. But moments before her jump, an instructor told her to keep her head up — a last-second direction she said left her little time to react.

Brandi Glanville also detailed suffering a perforated eardrum, concussion, bruised sternum and cracked rib after hitting the water during a helicopter challenge on "Special Forces." The show airs Thursdays at 9:00 p.m. ET on FOX. (Pete Dadds/FOX)

"My head hit the water. It was like a Mack truck – it, like, ran over my head. I thought that was it," she recalled. "And then a few seconds later, my body hits the water so hard. It was paralyzing almost. I was like, 'Oh my God.' But it was in slow motion."

The former "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" star said she suffered a perforated eardrum, a concussion, a bruised sternum and a cracked rib — injuries that forced her to travel by boat to the hospital because doctors didn't want her flying. Glanville recalled battling an intense headache on top of the excruciating pain from her rib injury, which made it difficult to breathe or cough.

Brandi Glanville said the painful experience ultimately made her feel proud for pushing herself and completing the challenge. (Tommaso Boddi/Getty Images for Rachel Strauss)

Once at the hospital, Glanville said doctors warned her she couldn't fly and told her she could be stuck there for at least two weeks and potentially need surgery. But after spending several days recovering and returning to the hospital for another evaluation, the reality star said she was determined to leave — even if doctors still weren't thrilled about her getting on a plane.
Battered but undeterred, Glanville said she still considered the experience a personal victory.
"Honestly, I'm so proud of myself. I feel like a badass, even though I didn't last long," she told Fox News Digital. "I went in, I conquered, I got hurt, and then I left and that was enough for me. "

title: Wendi McLendon-Covey fires back after Jeff Garlin blames bipolar disorder for 'The Goldbergs' exit

Jeff Garlin is opening up about his contentious exit from "The Goldbergs," saying his undiagnosed bipolar disorder contributed to the behavior that strained relationships with his co-stars before he left the hit sitcom.

The 64-year-old actor starred as the Goldbergs' family patriarch, Murray Goldberg, on the show from its premiere in September 2013 until he departed the ABC show during its ninth season in December 2021 amid HR investigations into complaints about his on-set behavior.

Garlin was accused by members of the cast and crew of inappropriate verbal conduct, unwanted physical contact, including hugging and touching, and behavior that some employees described as creating an uncomfortable work environment.
JEFF GARLIN DEFENDS HIMSELF FROM CANCEL CULTURE AMID ‘THE GOLDBERGS’ ON-SET CONDUCT ALLEGATIONS

While speaking with Vanity Fair at the time, Garlin denied intentionally harassing anyone. He acknowledged that HR had spoken to him over several years but characterized the complaints as stemming from his style of comedy and "silliness" on set rather than malicious intent.
He also said he was willing to adjust behaviors, like no longer hugging people.

Wendi McLendon-Covey is pushing back on her former "The Goldbergs" star Jeff Garlin's claims about his on-set behavior. (Noel Vasquez/Getty Images; Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for International Myeloma Foundation)

During a March 2023 appearance on SiriusXM's "Andy Cohen Live," Garlin's co-star, Wendi McLendon-Covey, who played his wife Beverly Goldberg on "The Goldbergs," said his exit was "a long time coming" and that "finally, someone is listening to us." She declined to discuss the situation further, saying she was "exhausted by that topic and the PTSD of it all."

On Monday, Garlin appeared on the Daily Beast's "Obsessed" podcast and addressed McLendon-Covey's comments and attributed his behavior to a mental health condition that had not been diagnosed at the time.

"It wasn't a long time coming for me," he said in reference to McLendon-Covey's past remark. "I actually empathize with her because, at the time, I was undiagnosed bipolar, and I was miserable on the show.

"I was miserable with my performance," he continued. "She was always trying to tell me, 'Hey, you're really great on the show.' I didn't believe her, and I just got to the point where I had to quit. She was very resentful, and it was a bit dramatic.

"I can only speak to what I'm responsible for," Garlin added. "Being bipolar, I was either one of three things: dark, dark, dark — where I didn't talk or look at anyone — happy to the point of mania, never turning off my thing or mean, really, really mean. I didn't know which one I was going to be. I didn't get diagnosed until I was 59. This was toward the end of my time on ‘The Goldbergs,’ so I could be a lot.

After his exit, the show completed some remaining Season 9 episodes using previously filmed footage and stand-ins before writing Murray Goldberg out ahead of Season 10. At the beginning of the tenth season, the show revealed that the character had died off-screen, allowing the series to continue focusing on the Goldberg family without him.

title: Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium concerts called off as troubled tour faces fresh setback
summary: Severe weather warnings forced Ed Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows to be canceled amid a backdrop of controversy involving Macklemore and Robert Kraft.
story: Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo discusses a fight that broke out on a flight to London and the controversy surrounding Ed Sheeran after Macklemore was dropped from his tour on ‘The Ingraham Angle.’
Ed Sheeran's concerts at Gillette Stadium have been canceled.

Sheeran was set to perform at the Foxborough, Massachusetts, venue on Sept. 25 and 26, but according to a statement shared on social media, potentially dangerous weather conditions have forced the singer to step back.

"Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium," Sheeran's tour promoter, Messina Touring Group, said in a statement. "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority."

Ed Sheeran's shows at Gillette Stadium have been canceled. (Deadline via Getty Images)
The company noted that refunds are available at the point of purchase. Gillette Stadium reposted the statement.

While the weather prompted the cancellations, the owner of Gillette Stadium, Robert Kraft, has been in the headlines recently due to the controversy surrounding Sheeran and one of the former openers for his tour, Macklemore.

After Macklemore used his slot at Sheeran's MetLife Stadium shows to express his support for Palestinians, many people were upset, including owners of stadiums where Sheeran was slated to play. The "Thrift Shop" rapper was eventually dropped from the tour, and in a lengthy statement reacting to the news, he wrote in part, "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues."

Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran's tour after using his set to speak about his political views. (Redferns)

"Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line."

Kraft wrote that he agreed with Macklemore that "too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering," but argued that "only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate."

title: '80s star Tiffany steps into dream role after leaving Hollywood behind
summary: Tiffany reveals her Off-Broadway role in "Spandex the Musical" fulfills a lifelong dream she put on hold when "I Think We're Alone Now" took off.
story: Tiffany Darwish told Fox News Digital that by 6 PM everyday, she is in the kitchen cooking before a peaceful night.
'80s pop icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight as she fulfills a dream she had prior to becoming a teen idol.
The 54-year-old singer, who rose to fame in 1987 after her song "I Think We're Alone Now" became a massive hit, made her Off-Broadway debut in "Spandex the Musical" last week.
During a July interview with People magazine, Tiffany reflected on why taking the stage felt like a "true full-circle moment for me."
'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD
"Before music came into my life, I was a dancer and an actor, and those dreams were put on hold when ‘I Think We’re Alone Now’ took off and my recording career began," she said.
'80s icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight to fulfill her lifelong dream after leaving Hollywood. (Bruce Glikas/Getty Images; Frank Hempel/United Archives via Getty Images)

Tiffany, whose full name is Tiffany Darwish, launched her career with the now-legendary Shopping Mall Tour '87, performing free concerts at malls across the country beginning in June 1987. The grassroots campaign helped turn the then-15-year-old into a teen sensation before she became a chart-topping artist.

In September 1987, Tiffany's cover of Tommy James and the Shondells' 1967 hit "I Think We're Alone Now" climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 less than two months after its release and made her a household name.

"I Think We're Alone Now" was the second single released from her self-titled debut album. She followed up with "Could've Been," the third single released from "Tiffany," which also topped the Billboard Hot 100. In addition, the album produced her Beatles cover "I Saw Him Standing There," which peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, and "Feelings of Forever," which reached the No. 50 spot.
Tiffany rose to fame at 15 with her hit song "I Think We're Alone Now." (Ron Eisenberg/Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)

At 16, Tiffany became the youngest female artist to top the Billboard 200 with a debut album. She went on to headline her first major tour in 1988, with New Kids on the Block opening for her before the boy band's own meteoric rise.

However, Tiffany's chart dominance proved difficult to sustain. While her 1988 sophomore album, "Hold an Old Friend's Hand," was certified platinum by the RIAA and produced the Top 10 hit "All This Time," it fell short of matching the success of her debut. As the teen-pop landscape shifted in the early 1990s, her third album, "New Inside," failed to gain commercial traction.
RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD

In 1993, Tiffany released her fourth album, "Dreams Never Die," which was issued only in Asian markets. Afterward, Tiffany largely stepped back from the mainstream music scene to focus on raising her son Elijah, whom she shares with her ex-husband, makeup artist Bulmaro Garcia. The two were married from 1992 to 2003.
In the early 2000s, Tiffany left Hollywood behind and moved to Nashville. During a 2023 interview with Fox News Digital, she explained why she decided to embrace a simpler life in Tennessee.
She became the youngest female artist to have an album top the Billboard 200. (Paul Massey/Mirrorpix/Getty Images)
DOLLY PARTON'S PATH FROM NASHVILLE NEWCOMER TO BILLBOARD'S NO. 1 COUNTRY MUSIC ARTIST OF ALL TIME

"I came to Nashville for the first time when I was 10," the California native recalled. "I’ve been coming back ever since. I love being out in the country – I’m a country girl at heart. I’ve toured all over the world and this place has always been home for me. There’s just something about coming home to my little ranch… I’ve never looked back."

Since the days of her teenage stardom, Tiffany has continued to tour and release music as an independent artist. She has also made appearances in movies and television shows and starred in several reality TV series.

During a June interview with Fox News Digital, Tiffany detailed how she spent the past several years building a culinary brand that combines her love of cooking, entertaining and connecting with fans. Through her platform, "Let's Food With Tiffany," she offers recipes, virtual cooking experiences and food-focused events that showcase the same energy and creativity that made her a pop sensation.

Earlier this year, Tiffany released her second cookbook, "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ‘80s Kitchen Encore," which she created with Las Vegas celebrity chef Alicia Shevetone. "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ’80s Kitchen Encore" followed her first cookbook, "Breakfast with Tiffany," which she released independently.
Tiffany left Hollywood for Nashville in the early 2000s. (Lorne Thomson /Darlene Hammond)

In July, Tiffany announced that she would make her New York theatrical debut in "Spandex the Musical," in which she plays Linda Gustafson, a housewife who competes in the fictional 1988 Crystal Light National Aerobics Championship.
"I’ve always believed the right role would find me, and the moment I read the script, I knew Linda was that character," she told People magazine at the time.

"Just as Linda discovers a new passion through aerobics that changes her life, I’ve found exciting new passions beyond music through my ‘Pop Life’ cookbook, ‘Let’s Food With Tiffany’ events, and now returning to acting on stage," she continued. "It’s a reminder that it’s never too late to reinvent yourself."

"Spandex: The Musical" is a 10-day limited Off-Broadway engagement which runs through Sept. 27. After each performance, Tiffany performs "I Think We're Alone Now" during the curtain call.
She is currently starring in Off-Broadway's "Spandex: The Musical." (Bruce Glikas/Getty Images)

"There are so many wonderful parallels between Linda’s journey and my own, and I’m thrilled the producers have even woven in some fun Tiffany Easter eggs that I know longtime fans are going to love," she told People.

Tiffany said the project is especially meaningful because a portion of the show's proceeds will benefit Children's Miracle Network, a nonprofit organization that raises money for 170 children's hospitals across the United States and Canada.

title: Forgetting names and losing keys may signal something other than dementia
summary: Dr. Tommy Wood breaks down memory's three neurological stages and why noticing your own forgetfulness is actually a good sign, not an Alzheimer's flag.
story: Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said minor forgetfulness is often caused by fatigue or stress rather than the beginnings of a neurodegenerative disease.

Everyday memory lapses, like misplaced keys or forgotten names, are often overinterpreted as early signs of dementia, but neuroscience experts say actual early cognitive changes may be reversible if addressed promptly.

Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said minor forgetfulness is often caused by fatigue or stress rather than the beginnings of a neurodegenerative disease.

"For most people, it's just because you're stressed or you're tired and weren't paying attention," Wood told Fox News Digital at Strong New York, the city's largest annual fitness and wellness festival.
DOCTOR REVEALS '10-YEAR RULE' FOR EVALUATING BRAIN FOG AND DEMENTIA SYMPTOMS
"If you want to remember something ... you need to actually be focused, be paying attention. You need to tell your brain it's important to remember it."
Understanding memory loss
Wood said memory formation works in three stages: encoding (forming a memory), consolidation (storing it) and retrieval (accessing it).
Cognitive changes during aging are not inevitable, and taking proactive lifestyle steps early can help maintain or even restore brain function. (iStock)
When someone is stressed or sleep-deprived, the issue is typically retrieval, he said — the memory exists in the brain, but the individual struggles to access it in the moment.
In contrast, people experiencing a neurodegenerative disease often fail to encode the memory in the first place.
‘MIRACLE ON THE HUDSON’ HERO SULLY SULLENBERGER REVEALS ALZHEIMER’S WARNING SIGNS HE MISSED YEARS AGO
"They don't even remember or notice that there's something going on," Wood said. "If you're noticing something's not quite right, that's usually a good sign."
Preventable risk factors and reversibility

Dementia is clinically defined as the loss of cognitive function that's severe enough to impair an individual's ability to manage daily life independently. Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia account for 70% to 90% of cases, with many individuals showing signs of both.
Research indicates that at least 50% of dementia cases can be prevented by modifying lifestyle and health risk factors.
True memory problems stem from a failure to encode new memories in the brain, whereas stress-related forgetfulness is merely an issue with retrieving existing memories. (iStock)
Key preventable risk factors include heart and metabolic health problems, as well as hearing and vision loss.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Wood emphasized that addressing physical health issues — such as obtaining hearing aids or undergoing cataract surgery — directly lessens cognitive decline risk.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"If you expect decline, you won't do the things that will prevent decline from happening," Wood told Fox News Digital. "Believing that it's possible means you'll actually engage in these processes, and then through that, you can prevent a lot of this decline."
Minor memory lapses, like forgetting keys or names, are usually caused by stress or fatigue rather than early dementia, the expert said. (iStock)

Wood's focus on reversible causes of cognitive symptoms aligns with guidance from Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic, which note that several treatable medical conditions can mimic early dementia symptoms or contribute to subjective cognitive decline.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Common reversible causes include the following.

Vitamin deficiencies: Low levels of vitamin B12 or B1, which are essential for nerve and brain functionEndocrine disruption: Thyroid problems, particularly hypothyroidism, which slows brain metabolismMedication side effects: Interactions from sedative drugs, anticholinergics or polypharmacy in older adultsMental health conditions: Depression and severe anxiety, which can cause "pseudodementia," a state of cognitive slowing and memory lapse that resolves with mental health treatmentMetabolic and kidney issues: Chronic kidney or liver failure, as well as electrolyte imbalances, which alter levels of brain chemicals
Vitamin deficiencies: Low levels of vitamin B12 or B1, which are essential for nerve and brain function
Endocrine disruption: Thyroid problems, particularly hypothyroidism, which slows brain metabolism
Medication side effects: Interactions from sedative drugs, anticholinergics or polypharmacy in older adults
Mental health conditions: Depression and severe anxiety, which can cause "pseudodementia," a state of cognitive slowing and memory lapse that resolves with mental health treatment
Metabolic and kidney issues: Chronic kidney or liver failure, as well as electrolyte imbalances, which alter levels of brain chemicals
Managing physical health issues — such as controlling high blood pressure, treating vision or hearing loss and staying physically active — directly reduces cognitive decline risks. (iStock)
Cleveland Clinic highlights that early clinical intervention is critical when individuals notice changes in "brain fog" or executive function.

"How your brain functions on a day-to-day basis is kind of the output of everything your brain is dealing with," said Wood. "But if you start to notice something, there's still time to make some changes if you need to."

title: 81-year-old refuses to stop working as wife battles cancer, then strangers try to help

story: Doorbell video shows 81-year-old Donald Johnson struggling to haul heavy suitcases up a steep staircase during a Texas delivery before his story spread widely online.
An encounter with an elderly delivery driver in Texas has captured attention after the reason he was still working came to light.

Donald Johnson, 81, was delivering lost luggage to a home when Erin Howell, a resident at The Colony, saw him struggling to carry a heavy bag up a steep set of stairs — a moment captured by her doorbell camera, according to reports.

Howell went outside to help and learned that Johnson had been making luggage deliveries as an independent contractor for the past three years to help cover medical expenses for his wife, Josephine Johnson, who is battling cancer, FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth reported.
MILITARY VETERAN’S PAINFUL WALK ACROSS AIRPORT TARMAC SPARKS STRANGERS TO RAISE OVER $135K
The couple has been married for 57 years. Donald Johnson continued to work during his wife's medical treatment.
He was continuing to make deliveries because he had struggled to find other work, he told Howell during their encounter.
Donald Johnson, pictured here, was delivering lost luggage to a home in Texas when a doorbell camera captured him struggling to lug heavy bags up a steep set of stairs. (TIKTOK/HelpDonRetire)
"It's the only job that will hire me," Johnson told her, according to the outlet.
Howell shared the elderly man's story online and even started a fundraiser to help with medical expenses and give him the chance to stop working and care for his wife.

As his story spread, thousands of strangers responded with donations and messages of support.
"I think I'm going to be able to stop working, and that's amazing," Johnson told FOX 4. "So we're not quite totally over the hump yet, but we're getting there very quickly."
Johnson was caught on video delivering luggage, pictured above, as an independent contractor to help cover the medical expenses of his wife. (TIKTOK/HelpDonRetire)
The outpouring of support and prayers had given her encouragement as she continued her cancer battle, Josephine Johnson told FOX 4.
"I can face it. I think that's the big difference," she said. "Some have made comments and they're praying for us. And it's just — it's a joyful feeling."

The family's circumstances, however, took another turn after the fundraiser was eventually removed from GoFundMe.

In a recent TikTok video, the couple's daughter, Amy Johnson, said the campaign had collected more than $700,000 — but that her parents would not receive the money because the donations were being refunded due to "a technicality."
The outpouring of support and numerous prayers from strangers had been encouraging the family in its battle.  (iStock)

Sitting alongside her parents in the TikTok, the daughter said the money that was raised was intended to help cover her mother's medical expenses as she battles pancreatic cancer and would also give her 81-year-old father the opportunity to stop working.

GoFundMe told FOX 4, however, that its trust and safety team determined the organizer account and fundraiser violated its terms of service. The company did not specify the exact reason for the decision.

Donald and Josephine Johnson, pictured here, discuss the overwhelming support they had been receiving. An online fundraiser begun by a stranger was intended to help cover the mom's medical expenses as she battles cancer and give the 81-year-old father the opportunity to stop working. (KDFW )

title: One simple lifestyle choice could help you live longer, says longevity expert
summary: Dan Buettner, founder of Blue Zones, says dog ownership may be the best longevity strategy, citing research linking it to fewer heart attacks and reduced loneliness.
story: Dog ownership is linked to a lower risk of early death, better heart health, more daily movement and less loneliness. Longevity expert Dan Buettner says a four-legged companion may naturally reinforce key Blue Zones habits.
The most effective strategy for prolonging life might be at the end of a leash.

Dan Buettner, longevity expert and founder of the organization Blue Zones in Minneapolis, Minnesota, highlighted a growing body of scientific evidence showing that owning a dog is strongly associated with a reduced risk of early death, particularly from cardiovascular disease.

"The best thing you can do to add years to your life may surprise you. Get a dog!" Buettner advised during a recent episode of "The Dan Buettner Podcast." "Research shows that dog owners live longer, suffer fewer heart attacks and experience less loneliness. Why? Because a dog forces you to walk every day, gives you a purpose and provides unconditional love."
LEADING ONCOLOGIST REVEALS 6 HABITS THAT COULD PROMOTE LONGEVITY AND REDUCE YOUR RISK OF CHRONIC ILLNESS

Dog ownership is associated with a 24% reduction in all-cause mortality for the general population compared to non-owners, according to research published by the American Heart Association in its journal Circulation.
For individuals who have already suffered a major cardiac event, such as a heart attack or stroke, living with a dog reduced the risk of death by up to 33%.
"The best thing you can do to add years to your life may surprise you. Get a dog!" a longevity expert advised. (iStock)
Epidemiologists and psychologists point to three reasons why canine companions may extend human lifespans.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
No. 1: Daily physical activity

Studies published in BMC Public Health indicate that dog owners walk an average of 22 more minutes per day than non-owners, making them significantly more likely to meet standard weekly physical activity guidelines.
Dog owners average an extra 22 minutes of daily walking compared to non-owners, making them more likely to meet standard recommended exercise benchmarks. (iStock)
No. 2: Stress reduction

Interacting with a pet lowers levels of cortisol — the body’s primary stress hormone —while boosting oxytocin, dopamine and serotonin. A 12-year Swedish study analyzing 3.4 million participants found that dog owners had lower blood pressure and reduced rates of cardiovascular disease.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
No. 3: Reduced isolation
The U.S. Surgeon General has declared chronic loneliness a national public health epidemic, comparing its health risks to smoking 15 cigarettes a day.
Dogs act as natural "social catalysts," fostering community interaction and providing emotional attachment that combats isolation, particularly in single-person households, experts say.
Dogs act as social catalysts that mitigate chronic loneliness, addressing a health hazard that the U.S. Surgeon General equates to smoking 15 cigarettes a day. (iStock)
The links between human longevity and caring for a pet aligns with principles found in the "blue zones" — regions of the world with the highest concentration of centenarians.
These key principles include natural daily movement, a strong sense of purpose, stress reduction and deep social connections, according to Buettner.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
By incorporating a dog into a daily routine, owners can incorporate these habits without having to engineer complex health regimens.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"So if you want to live longer," Buettner advised, "go adopt a dog!"

title: Scientists reveal surprisingly easy exercise that may boost your mood in just 10 minutes
summary: A University of Tsukuba study found that a slow 10-minute jog boosted attention, self-control and mood in young adults by activating the prefrontal cortex.
story: A University of Tsukuba study indicates that running at very slow speed can enhance mood and cognitive function. Dr. Jessica Gray, a family medicine physician, joins 'Fox & Friends First' to discuss the details.
It might not take an all-out sprint or long trail run to lift your mood and sharpen focus, according to a new study.
A new study from the University of Tsukuba in Japan looked at 24 healthy young adults who completed a slow, 10-minute run on a treadmill in one session and rested in another.

After the easy jog, participants performed faster on a test of attention and self-control and reported feeling more alert and pleasant than they did after the resting phase, according to the small study published in the journal Imaging Neuroscience in August.
'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS
Brain monitoring after the jog also showed more activity in parts of the prefrontal cortex, the area of the brain responsible for focus and decision-making.
The jog was purposely kept easy, with participants going at speeds from 1.9 to 3.7 mph on the treadmill. Their average heart rates clocked in at 105 to 107 beats per minute.
A small study suggests even a brief, easy jog may offer a short-term boost in mood and focus. (iStock)
"A single bout of running, even at very slow speed, elicits a pleasant mood and improved executive function," the researchers found.
SIMPLE BODY MOVEMENT COULD HELP THE BRAIN 'CLEAN ITSELF,' RESEARCHERS FIND
The finding "sheds light on the slow running benefits to brain health," they added.
Even gentle movement can provide a mental reset, though the study’s findings were limited to one short session. (iStock)
The benefits, they noted, stuck around even after participants' heart rates returned to baseline.
JUST 10 MINUTES OF DAILY FLOOR EXERCISES MAY IMPROVE BALANCE AND AGILITY, STUDY FINDS
The greater the up-and-down head movement during the jog, the more positive the participants' mood was afterward, though that finding was exploratory and does not necessarily prove cause and effect.
5 COMMON WALKING MISTAKES THAT COULD HURT YOUR PROGRESS, ACCORDING TO AN EXPERT

"Easy movement triggers the norepinephrine and dopamine pathways that wake up the part of the brain that is in charge of focus and self-control," said Dr. John La Puma, a California-based internist and author of "Indoor Epidemic," who was not involved in the study.
Brain monitoring during the post-jog attention test showed greater activity in prefrontal regions involved in focus and decision-making. (iStock)
Experts agree, however, that it does not mean one brief workout could be a cure-all.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"A brief jog should help someone get some energy in their system, which may make them feel better about themselves mentally and help them focus," said Dr. Scott Nass, a California-based family medicine physician at SwiftCareMD.
But Nass, who also wasn't involved in the research, said the effect is likely temporary.
Participants completed a test measuring attention and self-control after a 10-minute easy jog and after a resting session. (iStock)
For people living with depression or anxiety, a jog may briefly clear the mind but is "no substitute for medical care," he told Fox News Digital.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
The study was also limited in that it included just 24 healthy, young adults and measured outcomes immediately after just one exercise session.
The findings cannot be assumed to apply to older adults, novice runners or people with health conditions, and larger studies are necessary to confirm the results, Nass said.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
For a practical approach, La Puma suggested taking a 10-minute walk outside before the most mentally demanding part of the day.
Add 30-second jogging intervals, keeping the pace easy enough to speak in full sentences without becoming breathless, he said.
After the slow jog, participants reported feeling more alert and pleasant than they did after the resting session. (iStock)
People with heart disease, high blood pressure, Type 1 diabetes, recent surgery or joint pain should check with a clinician before starting a new routine, La Puma advised.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.
Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

title: Can faith help patients heal? Veteran doctor reveals what he's witnessed firsthand
summary: In his new book, "The Angels Among Us," Fox News contributor Marc Siegel reveals how 70% of physicians believe in God, and 55% report witnessing medical miracles.
story: Dr. Marc Siegel, physician and Fox News senior medical analyst, explores the intersection of spirituality, clinical treatment and unexplained medical recoveries in his new book, ‘The Angels Among Us.’

Dr. Marc Siegel, physician and Fox News senior medical analyst, explores the intersection of spirituality, clinical treatment and unexplained medical recoveries in his new book, "The Angels Among Us."
Examining how faith, human empathy and modern medicine converge during health crises, the book draws on medical research, historical cases and firsthand clinical experience.
"You don't draw the line between an explanation that's medical or spiritual. They're combined," Siegel told Fox News Digital. "And the more doctors that remember that, the better."
DR. MARC SIEGEL: 'THE ANGELS AMONG US' — A DYING WOMAN, THE SHOFAR AND THE MIRACLE THAT FOLLOWED
Siegel cites survey data indicating that 70% of physicians believe in God, and 55% report witnessing medical miracles in practice.

In the book, out in November, he expands the definition of "angels" beyond ethereal beings to include doctors, nurses and ordinary people whose timely interventions have led to unexplained recoveries or vital support.
Dr. Marc Siegel’s new book, "The Angels Among Us," examines how medical science, personal faith and human empathy intersect to produce unexplained health recoveries. (Fox News)

"The messengers are either actual angels from God that come down, that can take human form, that are voices where you don't have a visualization, or they can be humans that God appoints to do angel-like work," Siegel said.
"I started to identify humans who play the role of angels in our lives."
RUDY GIULIANI REVEALS HE HAD 'SPIRITUAL EXPERIENCE' WHILE IN PNEUMONIA-RELATED COMA
Among the cases featured in the book are U.S. Army Staff Sgt. Spencer Milo, who received a terminal brain tumor diagnosis after suffering severe trauma in Iraq.
While seeking a second opinion at the University of California, San Francisco, Milo met a Benedictine monk. Subsequent imaging revealed that the tumor was benign.
Survey data shows that 70% of physicians believe in God, and 55% report witnessing medical miracles in their clinical practice. (iStock)
Milo also credits former President George W. Bush with providing pivotal emotional support during a later personal crisis, identifying both as instrumental to his recovery.

Siegel references his residency training in intensive care units, sharing the story of an ICU patient who remained in a coma for three months following severe brain trauma. Despite receiving a negative prognosis, the patient unexpectedly regained consciousness and eventually returned to work.

"That embroidered on me the need to not give up, the need to look for explanations beyond just the purely physical," Siegel said.
"My role is not to decide who lives and who dies. My role is to relieve suffering and prolong life."

The book also includes personal accounts drawn from Siegel's own family, including his father’s four-year survival on dialysis via a catheter after surviving severe COVID-19 and complex emergency surgery at age 98.
Survey data shows that 70% of physicians believe in God, and 55% report witnessing medical miracles in their clinical practice. (iStock)
Other cases highlight sudden medical reversals, such as a critically ill ICU patient who reported seeing comforting spiritual figures just before her condition stabilized.
"My role is not to decide who lives and who dies. My role is to relieve suffering and prolong life."

Additionally, the book incorporates historical accounts, including an interview with Dr. David Gens, a lead surgeon who treated President Ronald Reagan after a 1981 assassination attempt. Gens detailed emergency room triage decisions, Secret Service dynamics and Reagan's recovery.

Siegel also discusses the origins of Alcoholics Anonymous, focusing on co-founder Bill Wilson's spiritual awakening at Towns Hospital in New York and the peer support model that followed.
Siegel emphasizes that while faith and prayer do not replace clinical care or guarantee survival, spirituality remains a key factor in patient resilience.

"Spirituality affects outcomes because it's a prerequisite to the courage to overcome," Siegel said. "Great doctoring helps enormously, but prayer and hope give patients the strength to keep fighting."
