title: ‘Storm fatigue’: Hawaiians reeling from back-to-back hurricanes as Nolo’s threats diminish
summary: A hurricane watch was in effect for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, which Nolo was expected to approach Tuesday,
story: HILO, Hawaii — Hawaiians have storm fatigue, Hilo’s mayor said Sunday, as the third hurricane to approach the islands in recent weeks continues to spin offshore.

The relatively calm state has been battered by the effects of multiple hurricanes, including Lala, Lowell and now Nolo, as the eastern and central Pacific have churned out at least 19 named storms. None of the three hurricanes has made landfall in Hawaii.
“So there’s storm fatigue and there’s some PTSD,” Mayor Kimo Alameda told NBC News on Sunday.

“I mean, you know, there’s a lot of anxiety around the weather now. You know, a lot of our folks out in the south side, they experienced, you know, catastrophic flooding,” he said, referring to the impacts of Hurricane Lala last month.

That storm killed two people, Alameda said, and damaged more than 200 homes without making landfall. Gov. Josh Green subsequently issued three disaster proclamations related to damage from separate storms in September alone.
Officials have reported some rescues but no deaths or major damage from Nolo.
“We did take some hits in some parts of the island,” Alameda said. “For the most part, we dodged a huge bullet. It could have been much worse.”

More than 120 National Guard members were activated on the island for Nolo, among roughly 400 statewide, after Green issued an emergency proclamation. President Donald Trump recently approved an emergency declaration, authorizing the Federal Emergency Management Agency to coordinate assistance and provide funding support.

In Nāʻālehu, at the island’s southern point, Peggy McKibbin surveyed silt-covered roads from her four-wheeler Sunday and pointed out the lingering damage from Lala — a bakery, a fire station and a hardware store wiped out.
“Everyone has been very much affected by this,” McKibbin said.
Nolo was a Category 4 major hurricane Sunday afternoon and forecast to strengthen, but the center was expected to remain south and southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
A hurricane watch was in effect for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, which the storm was expected to approach Tuesday, according to the National Hurricane Center.

The Pacific has been unusually active this season, according to National Weather Service lead forecaster Bob Oravec, with storm activity running above average during what is already the peak of hurricane season. He said the pattern is consistent with El Niño years, when the Pacific often gets more tropical storms and hurricanes.
Alameda, Hilo’s mayor, said people are ready if another hurricane comes their way.
“Unfortunately, we’ve been having a lot of practice,” he said, noting a recent tsunami threat and earthquake, as well as a precautionary eye on the volcano Kīlauea.

Mexico’s Baja Peninsula, meanwhile, was bracing for the arrival of major Hurricane Polo on Monday after it lashed parts of the country’s southwest coast with rain and strong winds. Polo remained a dangerous Category 3 storm with top sustained winds of 125 mph, the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami said Sunday afternoon.
Polo was moving to the north-northwest at 12 mph about 285 miles west-southwest of Cabo San Lucas at the peninsula’s southern tip, according to the hurricane center.

The Mexican navy said in a statement that it had gathered personnel and humanitarian aid in the ports of Guaymas and Mazatlán, on the Pacific Coast, and deployed three vessels that could ship aid to coastal communities isolated by the hurricane.
Also Sunday, Tropical Storm Rachel formed off Mexico’s southwest coast. Rachel had maximum sustained winds of 40 mph and was about 275 miles south of Acapulco. A tropical storm watch was in effect.
Ryan Chandler, Shanshan Dong and The Associated Press reported from Hilo and Dennis Romero from San Diego.

title: Benjamin Satterley, globetrotting wrestler known as Pac, dies at 40
summary: Satterley, who earned the nickname the “Man That Gravity Forgot,” had wrestled on pay-per-view Saturday night.
story: Benjamin Satterley, the hard-hitting and high-flying professional wrestler known to fans worldwide simply as Pac, has died, All Elite Wrestling announced Sunday night. He was 40.

News of his death came the day after he’d wrestled during AEW’s “All Out” pay-per-view Saturday night at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, outside Chicago. A cause of death was not immediately provided.

“A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” AEW said.

Satterley first began training at 18 and made a name for himself on the British independent scene before embarking on a globetrotting career in which he performed in some of the biggest promotions on the planet, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre.

But it wan’t until seeing the crowd reaction to one of his matches at a much smaller venue — Southern California indie promotion Pro Wrestling Guerrilla — that he finally thought he could make a career of professional wrestling.
At the time, he was still working night shifts at a courier factory, he told Colt Cabana in the “Art of Wrestling” podcast.
“I look back on it very fondly, but it was a tough time in my life,” he said.
Satterley arrived to WWE in 2012 to much fanfare. During his roughly six-year run with the company, he became the NXT Champion, NXT Tag Team Champion and WWE Cruiserweight Champion.
His high-flying offense, made all the more impressive by the brawny physique on his stocky frame, earned him the nickname “The Man That Gravity Forgot.”

That physique played a direct role in choosing Pac as his ring name. In an interview with Chris Jericho on the “Talk Is Jericho” podcast, he recalled having six-pack abs even as a kid. He would play fight with his dad, Satterley said, and his father would tell him to show him his abs, which eventually translated into a “silly nickname.”

When he started training and had to choose a name, Satterley couldn’t think of anything else. “It was only meant to be kind of a temporary thing, but then it kind of — it’s one of those names that kind of, it just stuck,” he said.
Satterley debuted on All Elite Wrestling in 2019, where he’d eventually earn the moniker “The Bastard.”

In AEW, he won the All-Atlantic Championship in 2022 and became one of the company’s more prominent wrestlers as part of the Death Riders faction, with whom he’d earn the AEW World Trios Championship alongside fellow members Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta in 2025. It followed another Trios title in 2022 alongside Penta El Zero Miedo and Rey Fénix as part of the “Death Triangle.”
Between the ropes, few wrestlers could combine speed, agility, technique and raw power quite like Satterley.
He could twist and wind his body off the top turnbuckle with his signature “Black Arrow,” or he could use his “Brutalizer” to tie up an opponent’s arms and neck on the canvas.
On the microphone, his promos conveyed no-nonsense intensity that relayed an ultimately simple message to opponents: I’m here to hurt you.

“My name is ‘The Bastard,’” Satterley said in one AEW promo. “The people named me that because I am a bastard. But on top of that — in addition to — I just so happen to be an excellent, exceptional, world-class professional wrestler.”
But that bravado belied a much shier quality outside the ring.

“I’ve got this kind of rejection complex, you know,” he told Cabana. “I fear failure, that’s kind of my thing. That’s kind of what holds me back in a lot of aspects of my life, especially professionally.”
Satterley grappled with his insecurities on the podcast but concluded that insecurities are part of human nature and that sharing them with the world could ultimately be a force for good.
“Maybe people can relate to the human side of me, rather than just whatever I do in the ring,” he said.
Tributes to Satterley quickly followed news of his death.
“The greatest export from our country,” fellow Englishman and AEW World Champion Will Ospreay said on X. “Also the greatest human being.”
“I am in shock. This is heartbreaking,” AEW wrestler Evil Uno said. “We have lost another great person, a great soul, a true professional.”
Ace Austin, whom Satterley defeated on a special episode of AEW’s “Collision” program Wednesday, summed up what many were feeling Sunday: “I don’t understand man.”
AEW referee Bryce Remsburg remarked on a decadeslong friendship with Satterley.

“To many, he was a bastard,” Remsburg said on X. “To my kids, he was Ben — who brought them Kinder Eggs from the UK, who converted them to Newcastle fans. To me, he was an incredible friend for 20 years.”
Speaking to fans during an indie show Sunday night, fellow Death Riders stablemate Marina Shafir said Satterley “was our bastard.”
“I was just holding this man yesterday,” she said, her voice breaking.
She recalled talking with Satterley about “wiener dogs” and basketball courts.
“He was just so modest about how fascinating he was. .... I wouldn’t be here today if I didn’t share time and space with this man,” Shafir said.

title: Europe frets as the Kremlin pushes the limits of its hybrid warfare
summary: The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.
story: The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.
After months of covert attacks and sabotage across the continent, leaders are warning that Moscow may be about to grow bolder as it seeks to sow chaos and intimidate allies of Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin could try to test NATO’s resolve to defend members on its eastern flank or respond to attacks that fall short of all-out war, these officials say, at a time when the U.S. is distracted by other conflicts and weighing reducing its military presence in Europe.

An assessment by the Danish Defence Intelligence Service released Thursday warned that in the coming months Moscow will further intensify its campaign of so-called hybrid warfare, “with greater consequences for the targeted countries than in the past.” It also assessed “a low but growing risk that Russia will launch a limited military attack against one or several NATO countries bordering Russia.”
While Moscow has for years embraced tactics that straddle the threshold of war, a string of increasingly brazen incidents in recent months has alarmed U.S. allies.
‘A bit freaked out’

A key moment was the discovery of a Russian drone carrying explosives at an airport in eastern Germany near a Ukrainian aircraft last month. Berlin formally blamed Russia for what it said was a thwarted attack and imposed a diplomatic freeze, though Moscow denied involvement.

That incident appears to have changed the mindset about Russia’s growing threat in Europe, said Ed Arnold, a senior associate fellow in international security at the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank. “It just showed that Putin’s risk calculations are getting more liberal,” Arnold said. “Everyone just got a bit freaked out by that, quite frankly.”
It was followed by the unexpected visit of CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow, during which NATO was discussed.

Incidents have continued to pile up — at defense facilities in Estonia, rail networks in Poland and the power grid in Germany. Many have passed without clear attribution, only intensifying speculation.
All this against the backdrop of near-daily drone incursions into European airspace, fueling anxiety in eastern border towns.

title: Inside NBC News’ polling averages: Democrats enjoy biggest lead yet in the race for Congress
summary: Meanwhile, President Donald Trump’s approval rating is at a low point for his second term.
story: Democrats are heading into the final stretch of the 2026 midterms with their largest lead yet in the race for Congress and President Donald Trump’s approval rating at a significant low, according to NBC News’ newly released polling averages.

A 9-percentage-point advantage for Democrats when it comes to control of Congress is part of a steady deterioration of the political environment for Republicans. The parties started the road to this November effectively tied in the weeks after President Donald Trump returned to office last year, but independents have gradually begun to prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress. And those voters have soured on Trump and his economic policies in particular.

The congressional average, which stands at 52% to 43% after adjusting to a likely voter scale, measures whether Americans prefer a Congress controlled by Democrats or Republicans before things like individual races and candidates come into play.

Individual polls can bounce around, but an average gives a broad sense of where surveys are trending, and it controls for outliers, which is one reason NBC News released our averages now. At a time when a flurry of polling is released, such as in the homestretch of an election cycle, averages can be valuable tools for tracking what’s happening in the election and diving deeper into how Republicans, Democrats and independents view Trump and the battle for Congress.

The NBC News averages are weighted calculations of all publicly available polls that meet certain standards for methodology and transparency tracking back to the beginning of the second Trump administration.
How NBC News' poll averages work

Our polling averages are designed to measure changes in public opinion over time, rather than reflecting the result of any single survey. They combine national polls using a statistical weighting method that gives greater influence to the polls that are most informative while reducing the effect of random variation from individual surveys.

Every polling average makes methodological choices about which polls to include and how much influence each should have. This methodology is used for both the NBC News presidential approval average and the generic congressional ballot average.
While the underlying calculations differ slightly to reflect the characteristics of each type of polling, the overall approach is the same.
Our approach emphasizes five principles:

Recency: Newer polls matter more than older polls. Precision: Polls with a lower margin of error are weighted higher. The margin of error can be influenced by the number of people in the poll and the amount of weighting needed to make the poll representative.Stability: Individual outliers and day-to-day fluctuations have limited influence until they are supported by additional evidence.Variety: Frequent pollsters have their older polls downweighted more sharply so that no one firm can dominate the average.Consistency: Polls measuring different populations are placed on the same registered voter scale before being combined.
Recency: Newer polls matter more than older polls.

Precision: Polls with a lower margin of error are weighted higher. The margin of error can be influenced by the number of people in the poll and the amount of weighting needed to make the poll representative.
Stability: Individual outliers and day-to-day fluctuations have limited influence until they are supported by additional evidence.
Variety: Frequent pollsters have their older polls downweighted more sharply so that no one firm can dominate the average.
Consistency: Polls measuring different populations are placed on the same registered voter scale before being combined.
Averages are not predictions. Instead, they aim to provide the clearest possible aggregate measure of the current available polling.

Polls of all adults, registered voters and likely voters are all eligible for inclusion, as are polls with a partisan affiliation provided those surveys meet certain methodological transparency requirements. Polls with partisan affiliations are noted as such whenever possible. NBC News collected all the surveys included in the average.

To be eligible for inclusion in the average, a polling organization must, at minimum, meet methodological transparency standards by reporting details on when a poll was conducted and how many respondents were interviewed. If a poll does not publicly release information on field dates, sample size and/or margin of error, it is not included.

Not every poll contributes equally to the average. Older polls gradually receive less weight as new surveys are released. Likewise, polls with smaller sample sizes or larger margins of error contribute less than more precise surveys.
Check out the full methodology page for the NBC News poll averages here.

With a month to go before the midterm elections, Trump’s approval rating has slid to 39% in the NBC News polling average, with 59% disapproving of his job performance so far. He began his term at 50% approval, according to the average.
Independents drive the shift toward Democrats
There has been little change over time among partisans in the race for Congress, with the vast majorities of Republicans and Democrats standing with their parties consistently.
As a result, much of the shift toward a preference for a Democratic-controlled Congress can be explained by the changing preferences of political independents.

Independents preferred Democrats by about 6 points at the beginning of Trump’s second term, and they slowly moved toward Democrats toward the first half of last year. But things began to shift more rapidly during fall 2025 and early 2026, moving to a lead of about 20 points for Democrats in the spring — as public frustration with Trump’s handling of the economy, the war in Iran and the killings of two Americans by federal immigration officers began to boil over.

The Republican Party hasn’t fully recovered with independents since, and Democrats now hold a 16-point lead among those voters in the race for Congress, according to the average. While survey responses don’t automatically translate into election results, such a strong showing among political independents is one of the many encouraging signs for Democrats heading into the election.

Even so, it’s no guarantee of electoral success for Democrats as Republicans seek to find a way to energize the coalition that sent Trump to the White House just two years ago and narrow the gap before Election Day, more than a month away. Republicans also hope they can defy the political headwinds because so many of the key battleground House and Senate races are being fought in districts and states Trump won in 2024, some by double-digit margins.
What’s behind Trump’s low approval rating
For Trump, movement among independents — and Republicans, to a lesser extent — explains his low marks from voters.

His approval rating among Republicans fluctuated in the mid-to-high 80s for the first six months of his second term, but now, his GOP approval rating is at 79% in a slight but noticeable decline, according to the average.
Independents’ approval of Trump has dropped further, to 26% in the NBC News average.

Voters have specifically soured on his handling of two of his signature issues — the economy and border security and immigration. In April 2025, an NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey found 40% of American adults approved of Trump’s handling of inflation and the cost of living, while 60% disapproved. By this April’s poll, 32% approved and 68% disapproved.
Inside the averages
Every polling average reflects decisions about which polls to include, how much influence to give them and how to account for differences in whom pollsters survey and how they go about it.

Some polls survey all adults in the U.S., which includes people who aren’t registered to vote or who aren’t eligible to be registered, such as recent immigrants. Other polls specifically survey registered voters.

A third set of polls — which become more frequent as the clock ticks down to Election Day — are polls of a population that pollsters identify as likely voters. Likely voter polls try to capture the attitudes of the group of people who will actually cast ballots, a moving target for polling organizations given the impossible task of predicting voter turnout exactly.

Those three sample universes produce slightly different results on our two key questions. Polls of all adults consistently show a lower approval rating for Trump compared with polls of registered or likely voters. Likely voters are likelier to have made up their mind on the generic ballot question about control of Congress, and as a result, both parties receive higher vote shares among that group.

Both our presidential and congressional averages combine those three universes by adjusting polls of adults and likely voters so they are on the same scale as registered voters. However, because the congressional ballot preference is a question about how people will vote, the congressional average shifts to show a likely voter baseline after Labor Day.

title: ‘Storm fatigue’: Hawaiians reeling from back-to-back hurricanes as Nolo’s threats diminish
summary: A hurricane watch was in effect for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, which Nolo was expected to approach Tuesday,
story: HILO, Hawaii — Hawaiians have storm fatigue, Hilo’s mayor said Sunday, as the third hurricane to approach the islands in recent weeks continues to spin offshore.

The relatively calm state has been battered by the effects of multiple hurricanes, including Lala, Lowell and now Nolo, as the eastern and central Pacific have churned out at least 19 named storms. None of the three hurricanes has made landfall in Hawaii.
“So there’s storm fatigue and there’s some PTSD,” Mayor Kimo Alameda told NBC News on Sunday.

“I mean, you know, there’s a lot of anxiety around the weather now. You know, a lot of our folks out in the south side, they experienced, you know, catastrophic flooding,” he said, referring to the impacts of Hurricane Lala last month.

That storm killed two people, Alameda said, and damaged more than 200 homes without making landfall. Gov. Josh Green subsequently issued three disaster proclamations related to damage from separate storms in September alone.
Officials have reported some rescues but no deaths or major damage from Nolo.
“We did take some hits in some parts of the island,” Alameda said. “For the most part, we dodged a huge bullet. It could have been much worse.”

More than 120 National Guard members were activated on the island for Nolo, among roughly 400 statewide, after Green issued an emergency proclamation. President Donald Trump recently approved an emergency declaration, authorizing the Federal Emergency Management Agency to coordinate assistance and provide funding support.

In Nāʻālehu, at the island’s southern point, Peggy McKibbin surveyed silt-covered roads from her four-wheeler Sunday and pointed out the lingering damage from Lala — a bakery, a fire station and a hardware store wiped out.
“Everyone has been very much affected by this,” McKibbin said.
Nolo was a Category 4 major hurricane Sunday afternoon and forecast to strengthen, but the center was expected to remain south and southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
A hurricane watch was in effect for the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, which the storm was expected to approach Tuesday, according to the National Hurricane Center.

The Pacific has been unusually active this season, according to National Weather Service lead forecaster Bob Oravec, with storm activity running above average during what is already the peak of hurricane season. He said the pattern is consistent with El Niño years, when the Pacific often gets more tropical storms and hurricanes.
Alameda, Hilo’s mayor, said people are ready if another hurricane comes their way.
“Unfortunately, we’ve been having a lot of practice,” he said, noting a recent tsunami threat and earthquake, as well as a precautionary eye on the volcano Kīlauea.

Mexico’s Baja Peninsula, meanwhile, was bracing for the arrival of major Hurricane Polo on Monday after it lashed parts of the country’s southwest coast with rain and strong winds. Polo remained a dangerous Category 3 storm with top sustained winds of 125 mph, the U.S. National Hurricane Center in Miami said Sunday afternoon.
Polo was moving to the north-northwest at 12 mph about 285 miles west-southwest of Cabo San Lucas at the peninsula’s southern tip, according to the hurricane center.

The Mexican navy said in a statement that it had gathered personnel and humanitarian aid in the ports of Guaymas and Mazatlán, on the Pacific Coast, and deployed three vessels that could ship aid to coastal communities isolated by the hurricane.
Also Sunday, Tropical Storm Rachel formed off Mexico’s southwest coast. Rachel had maximum sustained winds of 40 mph and was about 275 miles south of Acapulco. A tropical storm watch was in effect.
Ryan Chandler, Shanshan Dong and The Associated Press reported from Hilo and Dennis Romero from San Diego.

title: Madonna’s big night, Taylor Swift’s record and a Dolly Parton tribute at MTV VMAs
summary: LOS ANGELES — The MTV Video Music Awards made their West Coast return Sunday.
story: LOS ANGELES — The MTV Video Music Awards made their West Coast return Sunday. But like many Angelenos when they get stuck in traffic, the show was fashionably late when it aired on CBS.

A football game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys ran long, delaying the telecast by about 20 minutes. Many viewers complained that attendees and news outlets that were at the Peacock Theater were spoiling the roughly two-hour show by posting live updates on social media.
But the show went on after the telecast hiccup, with host Snoop Dogg keeping it running in a timely manner.
The rapper, a 13-time VMAs nominee and three-time winner, promised viewers that the awards would be “the biggest party the VMAs has ever seen.”
Here are some of the night’s biggest moments.
Madonna’s VMAs comeback
Madonna, 68, returned to the VMAs for the first time in 23 years to open the show, with help from Sabrina Carpenter and Charli XCX.
“It’s mother,” she announced as she graced the stage.
Carpenter reunited with the star to perform their dance track, “Bring Your Love,” which they debuted at Coachella in April during Carpenter’s headlining set.

“Brat” artist Charli XCX and Madonna also performed their single, “Danceteria Afterhours.” Their performance featured a slew of cameos, including actors Julia Fox, Julia Garner, Debi Mazar and Seth Rogen; record producer and songwriter Andrew Watt; fashion designer Tony Ward; and visual artist Fab 5 Freddie.
Madonna was nominated in 13 categories this year, the most of any nominee, for her album “Confessions II.” She took home three awards, including artist of the year.
During her last VMAs appearance, in 2003, she made headlines for kissing both Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera onstage, a controversial and iconic moment that made pop culture history.

Accepting the artist of the year statue, she reflected on her performance at the first VMAs 43 years ago, when, she said, her then-manager told her that her career “was over” after she experienced a wardrobe malfunction onstage.

“Seriously, I really want you to know that I spent the last year and a half finding myself, believing in myself and really making the music that I wanted to make,” Madonna said. “And to me, that really is the definition of being an artist. And my hope for all of you here tonight is that you spend the next year or the next 10 years or the rest of your life doing the same, finding yourself and believing in yourself.”
Late music legends honored
The death of Dolly Parton, known as the big-hearted “Queen of Country,” rattled the world last month, with tributes pouring in from fans across cultural, political, geographic and generational lines.
So it came as no surprise when the VMAs decided to honor the Hollywood legend, who died at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer.

Grammy winner Kacey Musgraves, best known for her “Golden Hour” album, paid homage to Parton on Sunday. She performed Parton’s hit “I Will Always Love You.” Footage of Parton appeared before Musgraves performed.
Taylor Swift later dedicated her award to Parton, calling her the “original showgirl.”
Later in the night, the VMAs also remembered pop superstar and Wham! band member George Michael, who died in 2016 at age 53.

The tribute featured performances from: Sombr, who sang “Faith” and “Father Figure”; Raye, who sang “I Knew You Were Waiting (For Me)”; Teddy Swims, who sang “Careless Whisper”; and Adam Lambert, who closed the set with “Freedom! ’90.”
Nirvana receives Video Vanguard Award
The VMAs never shies away from nostalgia. And this year was no different, with the awards show honoring Nirvana with its coveted Video Vanguard Award.
Surviving Nirvana members Dave Grohl, Krist Novoselic and Pat Smear reunited to accept the award.
The rock group’s last appearance together at the VMAs was in 1994, five months after frontman Kurt Cobain died.

“Nirvana continues to resonate so deeply because people are still hungry for authenticity,” Novoselic said onstage. “For something real, something uncompromising, something that tells you it’s just OK to come as you are.”
A big night for Taylor Swift
Getting married to NFL star Travis Kelce in July was not the only milestone for Swift this year.
On Sunday, she surpassed Beyoncé to become the most-awarded artist in VMAs history when she brought her Moon Person statue total to 32. Swift and Beyoncé had been tied with 30 VMAs.

The VMAs honored Swift with its inaugural Artist Director Honors, which organizers said was designed to celebrate someone “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling.”
Swift’s friend Dakota Johnson, the actor, described her as a “visionary” before she presented her with the award.
Taylor Swift becomes VMAs' first Artist Director honoree

“I got to start making music videos and being part of music videos 20 years ago, and since then I’ve gotten to be a part of making 60 music videos,” Swift said as she accepted the Moon Person onstage. “Eighteen of those I wrote and directed, and I really love writing and directing music videos. The main reason ... is because you, the fans, make it so much fun, you make it so rewarding, because you actually care about what we’re making.”

She thanked MTV and her fans before she debuted the music video for her song “Patient Zero,” which stars Johnson and Colin Farrell and was directed by Swift. Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki, known for “The Revenant” and “Birdman,” did cinematography for the video.

Swift surprised her fans last week by releasing brand-new bonus tracks from the “Showgirl” album, which she wrote and produced in Sweden with Max Martin and Shellback. In addition to “Patient Zero,” “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” tracks include “Cleveland!” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”
Swift was nominated in 11 categories Sunday for her “The Life of a Showgirl” album, which was released almost one year ago.

title: Benjamin Satterley, globetrotting wrestler known as Pac, dies at 40
summary: Satterley, who earned the nickname the “Man That Gravity Forgot,” had wrestled on pay-per-view Saturday night.
story: Benjamin Satterley, the hard-hitting and high-flying professional wrestler known to fans worldwide simply as Pac, has died, All Elite Wrestling announced Sunday night. He was 40.

News of his death came the day after he’d wrestled during AEW’s “All Out” pay-per-view Saturday night at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, outside Chicago. A cause of death was not immediately provided.

“A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” AEW said.

Satterley first began training at 18 and made a name for himself on the British independent scene before embarking on a globetrotting career in which he performed in some of the biggest promotions on the planet, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre.

But it wan’t until seeing the crowd reaction to one of his matches at a much smaller venue — Southern California indie promotion Pro Wrestling Guerrilla — that he finally thought he could make a career of professional wrestling.
At the time, he was still working night shifts at a courier factory, he told Colt Cabana in the “Art of Wrestling” podcast.
“I look back on it very fondly, but it was a tough time in my life,” he said.
Satterley arrived to WWE in 2012 to much fanfare. During his roughly six-year run with the company, he became the NXT Champion, NXT Tag Team Champion and WWE Cruiserweight Champion.
His high-flying offense, made all the more impressive by the brawny physique on his stocky frame, earned him the nickname “The Man That Gravity Forgot.”

That physique played a direct role in choosing Pac as his ring name. In an interview with Chris Jericho on the “Talk Is Jericho” podcast, he recalled having six-pack abs even as a kid. He would play fight with his dad, Satterley said, and his father would tell him to show him his abs, which eventually translated into a “silly nickname.”

When he started training and had to choose a name, Satterley couldn’t think of anything else. “It was only meant to be kind of a temporary thing, but then it kind of — it’s one of those names that kind of, it just stuck,” he said.
Satterley debuted on All Elite Wrestling in 2019, where he’d eventually earn the moniker “The Bastard.”

In AEW, he won the All-Atlantic Championship in 2022 and became one of the company’s more prominent wrestlers as part of the Death Riders faction, with whom he’d earn the AEW World Trios Championship alongside fellow members Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta in 2025. It followed another Trios title in 2022 alongside Penta El Zero Miedo and Rey Fénix as part of the “Death Triangle.”
Between the ropes, few wrestlers could combine speed, agility, technique and raw power quite like Satterley.
He could twist and wind his body off the top turnbuckle with his signature “Black Arrow,” or he could use his “Brutalizer” to tie up an opponent’s arms and neck on the canvas.
On the microphone, his promos conveyed no-nonsense intensity that relayed an ultimately simple message to opponents: I’m here to hurt you.

“My name is ‘The Bastard,’” Satterley said in one AEW promo. “The people named me that because I am a bastard. But on top of that — in addition to — I just so happen to be an excellent, exceptional, world-class professional wrestler.”
But that bravado belied a much shier quality outside the ring.

“I’ve got this kind of rejection complex, you know,” he told Cabana. “I fear failure, that’s kind of my thing. That’s kind of what holds me back in a lot of aspects of my life, especially professionally.”
Satterley grappled with his insecurities on the podcast but concluded that insecurities are part of human nature and that sharing them with the world could ultimately be a force for good.
“Maybe people can relate to the human side of me, rather than just whatever I do in the ring,” he said.
Tributes to Satterley quickly followed news of his death.
“The greatest export from our country,” fellow Englishman and AEW World Champion Will Ospreay said on X. “Also the greatest human being.”
“I am in shock. This is heartbreaking,” AEW wrestler Evil Uno said. “We have lost another great person, a great soul, a true professional.”
Ace Austin, whom Satterley defeated on a special episode of AEW’s “Collision” program Wednesday, summed up what many were feeling Sunday: “I don’t understand man.”
AEW referee Bryce Remsburg remarked on a decadeslong friendship with Satterley.

“To many, he was a bastard,” Remsburg said on X. “To my kids, he was Ben — who brought them Kinder Eggs from the UK, who converted them to Newcastle fans. To me, he was an incredible friend for 20 years.”
Speaking to fans during an indie show Sunday night, fellow Death Riders stablemate Marina Shafir said Satterley “was our bastard.”
“I was just holding this man yesterday,” she said, her voice breaking.
She recalled talking with Satterley about “wiener dogs” and basketball courts.
“He was just so modest about how fascinating he was. .... I wouldn’t be here today if I didn’t share time and space with this man,” Shafir said.

title: Taylor Swift surpasses Beyoncé to become most decorated solo artist in MTV VMAs history
summary: The “Life of a Showgirl” singer won the inaugural Artist Director Honors and video of the year awards Sunday.
story: Taylor Swift surpassed Beyoncé to become the most-awarded artist in MTV Video Music Awards history Sunday when she brought her Moon Person statue total to 32.
Swift and Beyoncé had been tied with 30 VMAs.
Swift won the coveted video of the year award for “The Fate of Ophelia” and dedicated the award to the late Dolly Parton, whom she described as “the ultimate showgirl.”

“Every single song that she wrote, her storytelling was so vivid and so rich,” Swift said onstage. “Listening to her songs, it’s like watching the best music video you have ever seen in your life every single time you hear what she has written.”
Taylor Swift becomes VMA's first Artist Director Honoree

Swift also received the show’s inaugural Artist Director Honors prize, which organizers said was designed to honor someone “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling.”
Actor Dakota Johnson, a longtime friend of Swift’s, presented her with the award, describing her as “an architect of emotional landscapes filled with the most intimate and intricate detail.”
Onstage, Swift reflected on the roughly 60 music videos she has made over the last 20 years, 18 of which she has written and directed.
“I got to tell you, though, the main reason why I love writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much fun,” Swift said after she thanked MTV.
The honor comes days after Swift released four new bonus tracks for “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,” a deluxe edition of her 2025 album, “The Life of a Showgirl.”
After her acceptance speech Sunday, Swift introduced the premiere of the music video for “Patient Zero,” one of the new tracks on the “Encore” edition.
The video, directed by Swift, co-stars Johnson and Oscar nominee Colin Farrell. Oscar winner Emmanuel Lubezki, known for “The Revenant” and “Birdman,” did the cinematography.

“With the Patient Zero video, I got to explore the cinematic and literary genres I love so much. I wanted to incorporate elements of gothic ghost stories, true crime, psychological thrillers all in a setting I hadn’t really shot in much,” Swift wrote on social media after the video’s debut. “The house was a metaphor for the coldness of a relationship that’s faded and atrophied.”
Following its midnight release Friday, “Patient Zero” broke the record for the most-streamed song by a female artist in a day so far this year.
The song and the accompanying “Encore” drop also gave Swift the most streams out of any female artist in a day in 2026.
Other tracks on the album include “Cleveland!” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

title: BASE jumper fatally plunges 700 feet after wingsuit failure in Utah
summary: Authorities described the 27-year-old man, whose identity wasn’t released, as experienced in the endeavor.
story: A 27-year-old BASE jumper died Sunday after his wingsuit failed when he launched from a 700-foot perch in Utah, authorities said.

The man, whose identity was withheld until his family could be notified, fatally plunged from a mountainous area of Hyrum, Utah, east of Millville Canyon and east of the small city of Millville, Cache County Chief Sheriff’s Deputy Doyle Peck said.

Search-and-rescue crews were called to Leetham’s Hollow, an area of canyon walls and cliffs not unlike the Grand Canyon’s, at 9:10 a.m. Sunday and declared the man dead at the scene, Peck said in a statement.
“On today’s jump, something went wrong and he did not have enough lift with his wingsuit,” Peck said. “He impacted the ground at a high rate of speed resulting in his death.”
The man was “experienced in this type of activity” and was part of a group of as many as 10 people who appeared to be engaged in wingsuit-aided BASE jumping, according to Peck.
The area, about 45 miles north of Ogden, is popular with BASE jumpers, he said.
A medical transport helicopter sent to help with the initial search transported the man’s body, Peck said.

Before Sunday, 541 deaths around the world since 1981 had been logged by the BASE Fatality List, maintained by an online community for the sport. This year, 15 such deaths have been reported globally, according to the list.
In June, two BASE jumpers died in a separate accident in Utah. One of them, Andy Lewis, performed onstage with Madonna at the 2012 Super Bowl.

Photographer Carl Boenish helped coin BASE as a description of the sport’s adrenaline-inspiring launch points (buildings, antennas, spans, earth) in 1978, when he videotaped early jumps from Yosemite National Park’s El Capitan rock formation.

title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
summary: Nor’easter floods the coast, a major incident is declared at a U.S. air base, and the Knicks on “Saturday Night Live.”
story: A powerful nor’easter battered the Northeast again on Sunday, flooding coastal communities and leaving tens of thousands of homes and businesses without power as forecasters warned that another round of high tides could inundate vulnerable shorelines.

The slow-moving storm, which killed a New York City Housing Authority worker when a tree fell Saturday, was expected to linger through Sunday with heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England.

The nor’easter triggered memories of Superstorm Sandy, which left behind over $60 billion in damage across the eastern U.S. in 2012. While this storm’s impact has been nowhere near that, it could be the first of several along the East Coast this fall because of an El Niño climate pattern that’s disrupting this year’s weather.
Officials said Hurricane Nolo still posed a risk for flash floods, dangerous winds and extreme surf in areas recovering from previous storms.

Nolo was churning very slowly south of the Big Island with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph. Its center was about 165 miles south-southwest of Hawaii’s southernmost point, and it was forecast to strengthen into a major hurricane late Sunday and early Monday while traveling westward to the south of the islands.
Five men arrested on terrorism charge near U.S. air base in Britain

British police arrested several men on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses on Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.
A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in west England.
The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base and arrested five men.
Asked about the incident, President Donald Trump told reporters the arrest was an “amazing job.”

In a Sunday interview on “Meet the Press,” Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., said the U.S. and China need to form a working group with technology experts from both countries to come to an agreement on AI.
“A lot of them can’t spell it,” quipped GOP Sen. Thom Tillis. Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego was equally skeptical: “They still don’t know how to get on the internet.”

One thing that everyone seems to agree on: Congress is not close to regulating AI. It hasn’t passed any sweeping, comprehensive legislation regulating the internet, invented more than 40 years ago, instead taking a more piecemeal approach and relying on existing laws.

Video showed Maricarmen Abascal, who uses a wheelchair, being taken out of the building in the Spanish capital’s Retiro neighborhood on a stretcher and driven away in an ambulance.

title: Nor’easter unearths fragments of 19th century shipwreck on Nantucket
summary: A local journalist spotted wreckage most likely belonging to the Warren Sawyer near where fragments believed to be from the doomed schooner were discovered in 2022.
story: The powerful nor’easter pummeling the East Coast has uncovered what may be the remains of a 19th century shipwreck on Nantucket’s shore.

Jason Graziadei, editor-in-chief of the Nantucket Current, spotted the wooden remnants on the Massachusetts island’s south shore Saturday and posted a video of them. He believes they likely came from the Warren Sawyer, a wooden schooner that wrecked near Miacomet Beach 142 years ago.
Nor'easter uncovers century-old shipwreck in Massachusetts
Fragments believed to be from the same ship first appeared in December 2022, when a Nantucket resident spotted them while biking along the island’s southern shore.

Researchers examined archival, photographic, historical and archaeological evidence and concluded that the wreckage was “most likely” from the Warren Sawyer, according to a 2023 report from the Massachusetts Board of Underwater Archaeological Resources. The three-masted schooner wrecked there on Dec. 22, 1884, while traveling from New Orleans to Boston with 1,115 bales of cotton and 28 tons of scrap metal, the report said.
More wreckage believed to be from the schooner appeared in February 2023, about a half-mile west of the first find, according to the report.

“As far as I know, it’s the first time a piece of the wreck has resurfaced since 2022, early 2023,” Graziadei told NBC News on Sunday. “It’s certainly possible it could be from another wreck, but given the location and appearance, we said it is most likely the Warren Sawyer.”

Jascin N. Leonardo Finger, deputy director of the Maria Mitchell Association, which runs a natural history museum on Nantucket, said in an email Sunday the newly exposed remnants may be from the Warren Sawyer, but “more investigation is necessary” to confirm their origin.
The Massachusetts Board of Underwater Archaeological Resources did not respond to requests for comment Sunday.

The Egan Maritime Institute, which works to preserve Nantucket’s maritime history and assisted the board in previous efforts to identify Warren Sawyer wreckage, also did not respond to a request for comment.

Shipwrecks near the island were not uncommon in the Warren Sawyer’s time, Leonardo Finger told The New York Times on Saturday. Nantucket residents commonly scavenge items that wash ashore from wrecks, she said.

title: Iran ‘fully prepared’ for war to resume but diplomacy not over yet, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says
summary: Despite Trump’s comments rejecting a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi said Iran hadn’t yet officially responded to the proposal.
story: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said his country is prepared to resume fighting with the United States but has not yet abandoned diplomacy after President Donald Trump publicly rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

“We are fully prepared for the time for the war to be resumed, and I repeat, we stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war,” Araghchi told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday, when asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Trump could seek to resume bombing after the U.S. midterm elections. “At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose.”

Iran had offered a deal last week to reopen the strait and resume normal maritime passage through the critical global oil chokepoint within seven days, as part of a plan conveyed to the U.S. through mediator Qatar on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Trump said Saturday that he had turned down that proposal, telling reporters: “I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly.”
Araghchi told moderator Kristen Welker on Sunday that despite Trump’s public comments, the rejection had still not been officially communicated to Iran via mediators.

He reaffirmed that Iran was ready to reopen the strait as part of an agreement to end the conflict, adding that in return, “we want our monies, our assets, which are illegally frozen, to be released. We want to be able to sell our oil.”

Araghchi said the conditions were “not new” and were things the U.S. has already committed itself to previously, referring to the memorandum of understanding that the two countries signed in June that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. That agreement collapsed within days after fresh strikes were exchanged.
“If you ask us, there is no reason why we should go back to diplomacy,” Araghchi said. “But I am still trying diplomacy because I think we shouldn’t miss any chance for peace.”
“We don’t care about U.S. midterm elections,” the Iranian official added. “We care about our national interests.”

Prior to Araghchi’s interview, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told “Meet the Press” that the deal was rejected for “a number of reasons,” suggesting the U.S. could not permit Iran “to have access to billions in frozen funds.”

Waltz said: “I think this was a pretty cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable, to ask for the release of the blockade, the sanctions, international sanctions and access to billions in assets.”
He also questioned “who’s calling the shots in Iran right now,” adding that the country had violated the past memorandum of understanding by attacking international shipping.

“I think it’s kind of common sense that the president doesn’t have a lot of confidence this time after we just tried a few months ago,” Waltz added. “What I can tell you is the president will leave all options on the table to ensure the world is safe from Iran holding the world hostage with a nuclear weapon.”
Asked what deal Trump would accept, Waltz said: “I’m not going to negotiate for the president.”
“This is about keeping the next generation safe from Iran threatening the world with a nuclear weapon,” he added.
Trump said last week he was still considering whether to “annihilate” Iran or make a deal.
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”

Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November midterms. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while 69% disapproved.

title: Bill Gates says getting countries to agree on AI regulations will be harder than Cold War-era nuclear negotiations
summary: The Microsoft co-founder said he believes governments should be involved in monitoring what AI does and that it won’t slow down the industry’s progress.
story: Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates called on the U.S. to be a leader in regulating the growth of artificial intelligence but warned that getting countries to agree on a global framework could be “more difficult” than Cold War-era negotiations to limit nuclear weapons.
“This is more difficult than that was,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Wednesday during a wide-ranging discussion on AI that aired Sunday.

His remarks came as he spoke about President Donald Trump’s stance against regulating AI. The president earlier this month rejected calls for the federal government to impose guardrails for companies building AI models, saying in a post on Truth Social, “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.”
Gates argued Wednesday that regulating AI companies by imposing monitoring systems would not hamper the U.S. in any race with China to develop superior technology.

“What he said is fine, but I think after he hears from me and other people, including that this does not handicap us in whatever he thinks the nation-state race is, that, you know, we will come to a consensus,” the tech mogul said.
Gates later pointed to other times the U.S. has led the world in coming up with broad agreements to protect humanity.

“Since World War II, the U.S. should be very proud that when there have been global challenges, we, in a way that was benign, where we had friends and allies coming along with us, you know, aviation safety, ozone layer, nuclear weapons, a lot of things where we played the fair actor, not aggrandizing whatever our unique strengths were,” he told moderator Kristen Welker. “And AI is one we’re going to have to go back to this, ‘Hey, humanity is all in this together.’”

Concerns about AI reached a fever pitch this month after Jacob Coxon, a whistleblower who had recently resigned from Anthropic, issued a public warning: “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Days later, two of the nation’s leading AI CEOs — Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Sam Altman of OpenAI — agreed there is a need to slow the pace of AI development amid fears the tech would soon be capable of “superintelligence” that outpaces human thinking.

In a blog post, Amodei wrote that “frontier” AI companies must slow down the pace of AI development but only to a point where the companies still lead China. He also urged global coordination between democratic and authoritarian governments to create regulations.
In a Sunday interview on “Meet the Press,” Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., said the U.S. and China need to form a working group with technology experts from both countries to come to an agreement on AI.
Banning self-improving AI models “should not be controversial,” he said, arguing that China also did not want to “lose control over AI models.”

“I do believe the United States can lead on a treaty that is both enforceable and verifiable, where we ban recursive, self-improving AI, and we have some monitoring of these frontier labs,” the congressman said.

In recent weeks, both Anthropic and OpenAI have announced plans to track the behavior of AI agents after OpenAI flagged multiple incidents in which its agents behaved in a concerning way, including by hacking an outside company without being told to do so.

In a post on Truth Social ahead of a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Trump wrote: “Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China’s position also.”

Following the Trump-Xi summit, the White House said the two countries established a dialogue to “exchange views on risks and benefits” of artificial intelligence. The next “exchange” is expected to take place by November.
Addressing immediate concerns about AI

While many have been calling for regulations that would limit AI from destroying humanity, Gates said on “Meet the Press” that he believes there should be guardrails in place to prevent mass-casualty events that could be coordinated with the help of AI today.

“The most dangerous thing we’re facing right now is people with bad intent using AI. You know, so somebody who wants to defraud an individual or wants to shut down the electric network or scramble bank accounts, they are now empowered,” the philanthropist said.

“Historically, countries had cyberattack teams and they could think of things like bioterror weapons,” he said. “Now, small groups with AI can do what only the biggest countries could do. So it’s really the bad intent plus AI that looms as a major threat. Unless governments insist on various safeguards, you know, we will see a lot of big, negative things because we’re not safeguarding.”
Gates specifically said monitoring, “where you’re watching what the AI is doing,” is an important safeguard to introduce in each AI lab.

“Law enforcement is going to get called up on all these fraud events or, you know, transmission shutdown events,” he added. “And their ability to see what’s going on is going to be nil unless the monitoring and safeguards are built into the AI.”
Plus, Gates said, these kinds of safety features can be added to current AI systems without slowing down the pace of development.

“That’s another debate — of should we slow down or not,” he said. “But deciding to put the safeguards and monitoring in, that’s a choice we have. And the only question is, Do we do that before or after there’s some large-scale cyberattacks or bioattacks?”
One bipartisan proposal in Congress would require a “kill switch,” or a way for AI companies to immediately suspend or shut down their AI services if a dangerous situation occurs.
Gates said “it’s not enough to have a kill switch” and renewed his calls for internal monitoring and safeguards.

“I would never want to say I’m against a kill switch,” he added. “But when you’re trying to moderate the bad behavior, you need insight and records of what’s being done. So the kill switch alone would not prevent these tragedies.”
The Gates Foundation and AI
The philanthropist, who now leads the Gates Foundation, also spoke about the group’s work expanding AI access to countries where English isn’t the primary language.

“AI models have gotten very good at recognizing English and about a dozen other mainstream languages. And so as you talk about your health, it’s going to accurately record that and be able to help you. In African languages, the error rate will be about 10 times higher,” he said, adding that errors can be “very dangerous.”
The Gates Foundation, he added, is working with 60 AI companies to expand the reliable languages they offer.

“We have a very concrete timeline to improve the quality, to benchmark and then say, ‘OK, this is good enough. You can do a health interview or an education session in this language,’” he added, saying he hopes that within five years every language that a million or more people speak will be close to the quality of English on these platforms.
Gates said his foundation is also using AI in its own work.

“It’s helping me in the foundation work,” he said. “You know, ‘What’s the latest on malaria? What’s the latest on malnutrition?’ It’s allowing the Gates Foundation, which will spend all its money over the next 19 years — you know, it’s got a bit over $200 billion — that money will be far, far better spent because we’re using AI to guide our work.”
A ‘regrettable’ relationship with Jeffrey Epstein

In the last year, Gates has also faced scrutiny for his ties to the late Jeffrey Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender. When the Justice Department released a trove of files related to Epstein at the direction of federal lawmakers, Gates’ name appeared multiple times, including in emails from Epstein suggesting that Gates had extramarital affairs.
The Microsoft co-founder has since called his past relationship with Epstein “foolish” and testified to House lawmakers in June that he did not engage in illegal activity with Epstein.
On Wednesday, Gates accused Epstein of using their friendship to boost his reputation.

“I was told by Jeffrey after I met him that he could help raise billions of dollars for global health — you know, he wouldn’t be paid, he would have no role. That proved to be a complete dead end. So my spending time with him, like many other people, kind of helped his reputation. You know, that’s very regrettable,” he said.

title: 6 towel warmers that will make your shower experience feel luxurious
summary: Make your post-shower experience feel more luxurious by heating your towel in a towel warmer — experts share what to look for when shopping.
story: Picture this: You’ve just finished a hot, steamy shower. You turn off the water and step out into the cold air. Not so pleasant, right? But now imagine that you’re wrapped in a warm towel. That picture just became a whole lot more luxurious, didn’t it?

A towel warmer can do more than just give you cozy vibes, says Michael Tidwell, CEO at Only Towel Warmers, an online towel warmer retailer. “A towel warmer can also serve several other purposes, such as warming the bathroom, drying towels for multiple uses and helping with mold and mildew caused by the wet fabric sitting around.” If you tend to really wet your towels after a shower, this could help you go through fewer towels in a week.

Additionally, if you have a pet that you bathe at home, a warm towel can make the bath process a little less uncomfortable for them. And towel warming racks can be useful for drying bathing suits and other items. So while a towel warmer can feel like it only serves the purpose of luxury, it’s also practical. To help you shop for one, I spoke to Tidwell about what features to consider, then sourced highly-rated options in a range of prices.

This four-bar frame works free-standing or wall-mounted  and includes hardware for both. It warms up in 15 to 20 minutes, drying towels, robes, and swimsuits while using less power than an average light bulb,according to the brand. The 7-foot power cord also has an illuminated on/off switch.
How I picked the best towel warmers

I consulted Tidwell for guidance to help you shop for a towel warmer. Since he works for a retailer that sells towel warmers, I did not ask him for product recommendations. Here are the features recommended to keep in mind when shopping for a towel warmer:

Type: There are wall-mounted towel warming racks and freestanding warming racks that you hang towels on. There are also bucket-style warmers that you place towels in to warm them up. When choosing between these, consider the space you have. A standing towel rack will take up the most space, whereas a wall-mounted rack will take up the least floor space. Bucket warmers take up a similar amount of space as a small trash can. Size: Towel warmers are mostly found in small and large sizes. Small warmers are intended for washcloths and hand towels (like the kind you see at a nail salon). In contrast, larger warmers can usually accommodate two oversized towels or three regular towels. For this story, I focused on larger warmers that accommodate bath towels. Is it okay to put wet towels in a towel warmer?

The short answer is yes, you can put wet towels in your warmer. Tidwell says a towel warmer can be a great way of preventing mildew from building up on damp towels that are lying around. That said, you should avoid putting soaking wet towels in there — damp is a better way to go. Unlike a dryer, a towel warmer doesn’t tumble the contents around, so there is no way to get enough hot airflow around a super wet towel to dry it fully.
Frequently asked questions

Towels come in various materials but are most commonly made with some type of cotton — a fabrication perfectly suited to a towel warmer. “Cotton towels hold heat well compared to [other] materials,” says Tidwell. “This makes cotton a great choice to use with a warmer.” As for other common materials used for towels, they should all be fine in a warmer. Linen towels tend to be a bit thinner, so they may not take as long to heat and polyester towels tend to be denser, so may take more time.

title: Love to Dream just recalled this popular sound machine
summary: Love to Dream recalled its portable baby sound machine over a battery fire and burn risk. Here’s how to check your model and date code and get a refund.
story: If you use a Love to Dream sound machine to help your baby drift off, you’ll want to pay attention to this news: The brand has recalled their portable white noise machine because its lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging with an incompatible charger, posing a risk of fire and burns. Below, find everything you need to know about the recall, including how to check whether your sound machine is affected.
Why was the Love to Dream sound machine recalled?

Love to Dream recalled its Sleep Machine because the device’s lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging if it’s connected to a charger that isn’t compatible with the unit. That overheating poses a risk of injury from fire and burns, a serious concern for a product that’s often kept in a nursery.

The recall applies only to the Love to Dream Sleep Machine with model number LTD-SM23 and date code 7W15TN. The recalled product is a white, heart-shaped portable white noise machine with a night light and a tan carry strap. You can find the date code printed on the side of the machine or on the back of its box, and Love to Dream says units with any other date code are not affected and aren’t part of the recall.

The affected machines were sold from February 2025 through September 2026, and Love to Dream is conducting the recall in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The company’s recall notice doesn’t say how many units are affected or whether any overheating incidents or injuries have been reported.
What to do if you have the recalled sound machine

If your Love to Dream Sleep Machine has model number LTD-SM23 and date code 7W15TN, stop using it immediately. Disconnect it from any charger and put it somewhere safe, away from anything flammable or anything that could damage it. Then visit lovetodream.com/recall to find out how to dispose of the device and claim your refund. Because the machine contains a lithium-ion battery, you should not toss it in your household trash or recycling bin. Instead, dispose of it only according to your local requirements for lithium-ion products.
If you have questions, you can contact Love to Dream by email at recall@lovetodream.com or by calling toll-free at 1-833-753-3710.
Other portable sound machines to use instead
The below portable sound machines have not been recalled and can be safely used.
Hatch Go Portable Sound Machine

The Hatch Go is a rechargeable sound machine for babies on the go. It plays 10 soothing sounds, like white noise and heartbeat, and has three buttons plus a ring to clip onto a stroller or diaper bag. It needs no app, WiFi or Bluetooth, and lasts up to 15 hours per charge.
Yogasleep Hushh Portable White Noise Sound Machine

The Yogasleep Hushh is a compact portable sound machine with three sounds: bright white noise, deep white noise and gentle surf. It weighs just 3.8 ounces, has an amber night light and child lock, and clips onto a stroller, car seat or crib. It runs up to 24 hours per charge.
Momcozy Portable Sound Machine with Night Light

With 20 soothing sounds and an amber night light you can dim, this portable machine from Momcozy works for nursery and travel alike. It clips onto a stroller, crib or diaper bag, and includes a timer, child lock and auto shut-off. It charges via USB-C and is designed to last all night.

title: BASE jumper fatally plunges 700 feet after wingsuit failure in Utah
summary: Authorities described the 27-year-old man, whose identity wasn’t released, as experienced in the endeavor.
story: A 27-year-old BASE jumper died Sunday after his wingsuit failed when he launched from a 700-foot perch in Utah, authorities said.

The man, whose identity was withheld until his family could be notified, fatally plunged from a mountainous area of Hyrum, Utah, east of Millville Canyon and east of the small city of Millville, Cache County Chief Sheriff’s Deputy Doyle Peck said.

Search-and-rescue crews were called to Leetham’s Hollow, an area of canyon walls and cliffs not unlike the Grand Canyon’s, at 9:10 a.m. Sunday and declared the man dead at the scene, Peck said in a statement.
“On today’s jump, something went wrong and he did not have enough lift with his wingsuit,” Peck said. “He impacted the ground at a high rate of speed resulting in his death.”
The man was “experienced in this type of activity” and was part of a group of as many as 10 people who appeared to be engaged in wingsuit-aided BASE jumping, according to Peck.
The area, about 45 miles north of Ogden, is popular with BASE jumpers, he said.
A medical transport helicopter sent to help with the initial search transported the man’s body, Peck said.

Before Sunday, 541 deaths around the world since 1981 had been logged by the BASE Fatality List, maintained by an online community for the sport. This year, 15 such deaths have been reported globally, according to the list.
In June, two BASE jumpers died in a separate accident in Utah. One of them, Andy Lewis, performed onstage with Madonna at the 2012 Super Bowl.

Photographer Carl Boenish helped coin BASE as a description of the sport’s adrenaline-inspiring launch points (buildings, antennas, spans, earth) in 1978, when he videotaped early jumps from Yosemite National Park’s El Capitan rock formation.

title: Third suspect arrested in death of Mississippi woman found hanging at ‘staged’ crime scene
summary: Two other people, Earnest Lloyd Jr. and Jarques Ratliff, were also arrested and charged with murder in connection with Tasia Fortune’s death.
story: A third person has been arrested in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old woman who police said was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned Mississippi home in August.
Eric Clark, 45, surrendered to police on Friday and is charged with murder. Police also disclosed on Friday that according to an autopsy investigation, “the scene and the hanging were staged.”
No other details were released about the scene or Fortune’s killing.
Clark is expected to appear in court on Monday.
Two other people, Earnest Lloyd Jr. and Jarques Ratliff, were also arrested and charged with murder in connection with her death. Both men are Black.

Police have released very little information about what led up to Fortune’s death. Detectives investigating the case have interviewed as many as 15 people, collected forensic evidence and followed numerous leads, police said in a news release.
Authorities said Ratliff, 51, had an “association” with Fortune but did not release further details.

Lloyd, 25, allegedly had a physical altercation with Fortune either days or minutes before she died, according to NBC affiliate WLBT of Jackson. Police accused Lloyd of hanging Fortune with a black cable cord, WLBT reported.
Ratliff, who pleaded not guilty, and Lloyd were denied bond at separate court hearings.

title: Adam Lambert Shocks Crowd With Surprise Performance During VMAs George Michael Tribute
summary: The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
story: Surprise!

The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
The homage comes a decade after the pop legend and queer icon died on Christmas Day 2016 at age 53.
Lambert, joined by several other artists including singer Meek and MNEK, belted out the 1990 hit. Several in the crowd were brought to their feet during the performance.

The tribute also featured Sombr, who performed Michael’s hit songs “Faith” and “Father Figure,” Raye, who performed “Knew You Were Waiting,” and Teddy Swims who sang a rendition of “Careless Whisper.”
During his portion, Sombr also wore a black Harley-Davidson jacket that originally worn by Michael during his 1988 Faith Tour, according to Vogue.
“To wear a jacket that has become so synonymous with that era was pretty surreal, and an honor,” Sombr told the magazine.

Michael, who won a host of VMAs, including the Video Vanguard lifetime achievement award in 1989, was highly regarded as a pioneering artist in the pop music scene, making a significant impact both as one-half of the duo Wham! and also as a solo artist.
While the icon was known for his many musical hits, he is also remembered as a champion of the LGBTQ+ community and philanthropist, who used his platform to help find a cure for HIV and AIDS.

Michael was outed as gay in 1998 following an incident in Beverly Hills during which he was arrested for engaging in a lewd act at a public toilet. Michael later roasted the ordeal in his music video for “Outside,” in which he mocked the Los Angeles police officers who caught him by featuring two uniformed officers kissing.

“I’m a very proud man. I want people to know that I have not been exposed as a gay man,” Michael told CNN in a now-famous 1998 interview. “I don’t feel any shame whatsoever, and neither do I think I should.”
With his unapologetic embrace of his sexuality, the musician is credited with opening the door and empowering many other queer entertainers in the music industry.

Given his rich legacy, many fans initially called out the VMAs for its choice in tribute performers — none of whom had publicly identified as a member of the LGBTQ+ community. MTV had announced exclusively in Rolling Stone Sept. 22 that acts Raye, Sombr and Teddy Swims would be performing. Many felt that without performers who reflected Michael’s activism and identity, the LGBTQ community was being snubbed.

“You’d think with George being an icon for the LGBT community, they’d get someone like Sam Smith or Troye Sivan involved,” one user wrote on social media platform Reddit, referencing other openly gay pop icons.
While no other artists were announced ahead of the awards, singer Adam Lambert posted a cryptic Instagram story which featured Michael’s song “Freedom ‘90.”
