title: A Brief History of Madonna and the VMAs, Going Back to 1984: ‘The House She Helped Build’
summary: Madonna is returning to the VMAs. What is Madonna’s history with the VMAs?
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Where would the MTV Video Music Awards be without Madonna?

Madonna’s name is practically synonymous with the VMAs. She was there from the beginning, rolling around the stage in a wedding dress while performing “Like A Virgin” during the awards show’s 1984 debut.

Over the next four decades, Madonna returned to the VMAs to deliver groundbreaking performances. She’s also made headlines with outrageous antics — like French kissing Britney Spears onstage — and touched fans’ hearts with an emotional tribute to Michael Jackson after the musician’s death in 2009.
Now, the Queen of Pop is poised make a historic return to the 2026 VMAs on Sept. 27 when she performs at the awards show for the first time in 23 years.
Madonna’s performance will kick off the awards show for a record-breaking fifth time, ending her tie with Rihanna, who’s opened the show four times.
Madonna who released her hit album, “Confessions II,” in July, also goes into this year’s VMAs as the most nominated performer.
The singer is “returning to sit on her throne for the night,” NBC News entertainment contributor Chris Witherspoon tells TODAY.com.

“You simply cannot tell the story of the VMAs without telling the story of Madonna. From ‘Like a Virgin’ in 1984, to ‘Vogue’ in 1990, to that unforgettable 2003 performance with Britney Spears, Christina Aguilera and Missy Elliott, Madonna understood the assignment before we even had the phrase,” said Witherspoon.
“Madonna returning to the VMAs doesn’t feel like a comeback to me. It feels like the Queen of Pop returning to the house she helped build,” Witherspoon added.
Ahead of Madonna’s triumphant VMAs return, let’s take a look back at her 10 biggest moments at the awards show.
1) The Wedding Dress Seen Round the World (1984)

Madonna’s audacious performance at the inaugural MTV Video Music Awards in 1984 — she rolled around the stage in a punky ensemble that includes a wedding dress, rosary beads and a “Boy Toy” belt buckle — became her breakout moment.
The raunchy performance, which also included some bumping and grinding, also branded the VMAs as a rebellious alternative to the Grammys and other awards shows.

“MTV could barely fill the seats at the VMAs in year one. By year two, pretty much every act wanted a spot on that stage. Madonna was at the first show in 1984, rolling across the stage in a wedding dress singing ‘Like a Virgin.’ I’d give her a lot of credit for that turnaround,” Jeff Moore, a music marketing strategist, professor, and former touring musician, told TODAY.com.
2) Madonna Expresses Herself (1989)
Madonna returned to the VMAs five years later to deliver one of her finest televised performances when she sang “Express Yourself” with her two backup singers-dancers.

The newly divorced singer — her marriage to Sean Penn officially ended earlier in the year —  began her high-energy, tightly choreographed performance wearing a dark suit before stripping down to a corset.
3) ‘Vogue’ Meets the French Revolution (1990)

The former Material Girl’s breathtaking 1990 performance of “Vogue” was inspired by the French Revolution. Madge as Marie Antoinette? Oh, it worked, right down to her and her dancers’ 18th century-style powdered wigs, heavy white face makeup and corseted gowns.
4) ‘Ray of Light’ with Lenny Kravtiz (1998)
In what’s considered one of the best live performances, Madonna showed off her vocal chops on the soaring “Ray of Light’ with guest guitarist Lenny Kravitz during the 1998 show.
The singer, who kicked off the performance with the Hindu-inspired  “Shanti Ashtangi,” also swept the awards that night, taking home five Moon Man trophies.
5) Madonna Meets Her Drag Impersonators (1999)
The singer was feted the following year by a group of drag queens who wore some of her most memorable looks as they lip-synched and danced to her greatest hits.
“All I have to say is that it takes a real man to fill my shoes!” the singer quipped afterwards.
6) Kissing Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera (2003)
In 2003, Madonna shocked viewers when she took a moment during a throwback performance of “Like A Virgin” to kiss shared her guest performers Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.
Spears and Aguilera donned skimpy wedding dress looks in a fun nod to Madonna’s debut VMAs performance.
7) An Emotional Tribute to Michael Jackson (2009)

Madonna showed off her serious side when she paid an emotional tribute to her late fellow pop icon Michael Jackson at the 2009 VMAs, calling Jackson “one of the greatest talents the world has ever known.”

“His music,” she said in her speech, “had an extra layer of inexplicable magic that didn’t just make you want to dance but actually made you believe you could fly, dare to dream, be anything that you wanted to be.”
She also recalled going to dinner with Jackson years before.

“Later we went back to my house to watch a movie and sat on the couch like two kids, and somewhere in the middle of the movie, his hand snuck over and held mine,” she said. “It felt like he was looking for more of a friend than a romance, and I was happy to oblige. In that moment, he didn’t feel like a superstar. He felt like a human being.”
8) A Surprise Appearance, Motherf-----! (2021)
Decked out out black dominatrix bodysuit and cap, Madonna made a surprise appearance to open the 2021 VMAs.
The singer’s appearance came just after viewers watched a short video telling the story of her arrival in New York City decades before with just $35 to her name.
Madonna then walked out onstage, telling the crowd, “And they said we wouldn’t last. But we’re still here, motherf------!”

title: Taylor Swift Reflects on Her 60 Music Videos While Accepting the Inaugural Artist Director Honors at the VMAs
summary: What did Taylor Swift say in her speech while accepting the inaugural Artist Director Honors at the 2026 VMAs?
story: Taylor Swift already has 30 VMAs. At the 2026 ceremony, she racked up another honor, and she was the first to ever receive it: the Artist Director Honors.
The pop icon was presented the award by friend Dakota Johnson, who celebrated the “visionary with a relentless drive for perfection for everything she does.”

Viewers and the audience then watched a clip of behind-the-scenes of Swift bringing the ideas to the screen. Swift talked through her thought process and said, “I think I will always want to tell human stories about human emotion.”
In her speech during the ceremony on Sept. 27, she reflected on making “roughly” 60 music videos throughout her decades-long career, including 18 that she wrote and directed.

“I’ve got to tell you though the main reason why I love writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much fun,” she said as the crowd erupted into cheers and applause.
She said she finds the experience “so rewarding” before thanking every person who has contributed to her music videos, adding that she learned something from all of them.
Swift concluded her speech by again expressing her gratitude for his fans before unveiling her latest masterpiece: the music video for new single “Patient Zero.”

The VMAs previously shared in a press release that the special honor was created to recognize “groundbreaking music artists whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling.”
Swift had an eventful evening. The awards show came two days after she released four new songs as part of her “The Life of the Showgirl: The Encore” album.
The music video for one of the new songs, “Patient Zero,” debuted at the VMAs after her speech.
She proudly watched the clip with Johnson, who starred in the music video, by her side.

The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards are being hosted by Snoop Dogg at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Madonna leads with 11 nominations. The show will feature special presentations, like the MTV VMA Artist Director Honors and Video Vanguard Award. Taylor Swift, who received nine nominations, will receive the Artist Director Honors award and debut the music video for her new single “Patient Zero.” The ceremony will include tributes to Dolly Parton and George Michael, as well.

title: Vintage Dolly Parton Footage Kicks Off Her VMAs Tribute as Kacey Musgraves Honors Late Legend
summary: Kacey Musgraves honored the late Dolly Parton with a tribute during the VMAs 2026, which kicked off with a cameo from Dolly herself.
story: Leave it to Dolly Parton to make us sob — even in absentia.

The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to the queen of country in a stunning homage that began with a cameo from Parton herself. It comes weeks after the “Jolene” singer died on Aug. 25 at the age of 80.

The tribute, which featured a cover of Parton’s hit “I Will Always Love You,” sung by Kacey Musgraves, included several clips of Parton speaking to the audience.
Musgraves, dressed in a sparkling mauve dress, also impressed the crowd with her stunning vocals.
The segment was met with a critical acclaim from fans of Parton, who praised the awards ceremony for putting together a tasteful tribute.
“this had me sobbing. genuinely, kacey did such a beautiful tribute to dolly🦋” one person wrote on platform X.
Another person wrote that they were “not ok” after seeing the emotional performance.
Dolly Parton’s death sent shockwaves across the nation. The beloved star was known for both her plethora of country hits as well as her major philanthropic efforts.

story: “It’s mother!”
Madonna made her grand return to the MTV Video Music Awards with an epic performance of her newest hits, and help from Sabrina Carpenter and Charli XCX
The queen of pop graced the stage to open the 2026 VMAs on Sunday, Sept. 27, marking the first time she has performed at the award show in 23 years.
To kick things off, Madonna was joined by Carpenter to sing their dance duet “Bring Your Love.” Madonna stood on top of a piano while Carpenter played the keys.
They then started to strut around the stage while surrounded by a group of dancers.
Next, it was time for a wardrobe change for Madonna before she was transported to a second stage with a veiled choir.

For the grand finale, Madonna introduced Charli XCX before the two sang along to “Danceteria Afterhours,” a remix from the music icon’s most recent album “Confessions II.” As they belted the lyrics, celebrities like Sombr,  Debi Mazar and Julia Garner, who was previously tapped to play Madonna in a biopic, made appearances.

Tonight, all eyes are on Madonna, who released her 15th studio album, “Confessions II,” in July, as she is the most nominated performer. She earned 13 nominations, including for video of the year and artist of the year.

Her opening is now added to the list of unforgettable performances Madonna has had at the award show. She has drawn eyes to the VMAs since they began in 1984. That year, she rolled around on the stage in a wedding dress while singing “Like a Virgin.”
She shared the stage and kisses with Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera at the 2003 ceremony, and in 2009 she delivered an emotional tribute to Michael Jackson shortly after his death.

“Madonna returning to the VMAs doesn’t feel like a comeback to me. It feels like the Queen of Pop returning to the house she helped build,” NBC News entertainment contributor Chris Witherspoon told TODAY.com ahead of her performance.
We’ll be watching tonight to see if she can add a few more Moon Person trophies to her collection of accolades.

story: Taylor Swift is back at the VMAs for the first time in two years. She arrived at the red carpet shortly before the award show’s 7:30  p.m. ET start time wearing a sleek black and silver dress.

The Tamara Ralph couture gown started with a tight-fitted black bodice and a high neck, before transitioning into a cascading, shimmering skirt. She paired it with long earrings and her new shorter haircut.

The contrasting vibe of the dress seems to be a nod to the “Patient Zero” music video, which she’s debuting in full at the 2026 VMAs. The music video’s somber and dark visuals were already teased ahead of the show, and accompany lyrics about a toxic relationship.

Her husband, Travis Kelce, wasn’t with her at the red carpet, as he has a football game against the Miami Dolphins in Florida at the same time as the VMAs.
Swift was last at the awards show in 2024, rounding out an eventful three-year span in which she announced surprise albums and swept categories.

Swift wore a yellow-and-black plaid get-up to her last VMAs in 2024, where she was up for 12 awards. Swift won seven awards that night, and thanked her now-husband Kelce in her speech for video of the year.
“Everything this man touches turns to happiness and fun and magic,” she said. “So I want to thank him for adding that to our shoot because I will always remember that.”
The year before, in 2023, Swift had another astonishing VMAs, tying the record for most wins in one night.
And in 2022, she made a surprise appearance and announced a new album.

title: Jalen Brunson Shines as A Transfer Student in Hilarious ‘SNL’ Spoof of ‘High School Musical’
summary: During the Sept. 26 season premiere of “Saturday Night Live,” host Jalen Brunson starred in a spoof of “High School Musical” as a shy new transfer student.
story: Move over, Troy and Chad. There’s a new baller in town.

During the Sept. 26 season premiere of “Saturday Night Live,” host Jalen Brunson starred as a shy new transfer student in a spoof of Disney Channel’s “High School Musical.” And let’s just say things turn around for the new kid pretty quickly.
Brunson hosted the Season 52 premiere while girl group KATSEYE served as the musical guest.

In the sketch “High School Musical the New Generation,” transfer student Brunson looks to join the school basketball team. “SNL” featured player Jeremy Culhane greets the new guy with a parody of “Get’cha Head in the Game” from the actual “High School Musical” movie.
“Of course, you can ball with us. But know this,” Culhane says in the sketch. “When you’re at North High, you got to give it all you got!”
Unfortunately, Culhane has none of the luck that Troy Bolton did in the original franchise, with each of his scoring attempts blocked by none other than Brunson.
Brunson ends up absolutely dominating Culhane and by the end of the skit, the Knicks captain also steals Culhane’s love interest, played by Veronika Slowikowska.
Brunson’s appearance on the sketch show made him the fifth NBA player to host “SNL.” The others were coach Bill Russell and NBA icons Michael Jordan, Charles Barkley and LeBron James.

The Knicks captain had some familiar friends join him for his episode as well. The other members of the starting five, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Karl-Anthony Towns made cameos amid Brunson’s opening monologue.

The eventful night follows the Knicks’ NBA title win in June, which ended the team’s 53-year-long championship drought. During the Finals, Brunson averaged an impressive 32.6 points per game and cemented his status as the reigning “King of New York.”

title: Jalen Brunson Gets A Big Assist From Knicks Teammates In ‘SNL’ Opening Monologue
summary: “Saturday Night Live” host and reigning King of New York Jalen Brunson got by with a little help from his friends during his big moment on the sketch show.
story: “Saturday Night Live” host and reigning King of New York Jalen Brunson got by with a little help from his friends during his big moment on the sketch show.

Brunson, captain of the New York Knicks, delivered an opening monologue Sept. 26 that heavily referenced the team’s NBA title-winning run this year. But of course, it wasn’t complete without an appearance from the rest of his fellow now-iconic Knicks starting five.
Brunson’s episode marked the Season 52 premiere of “SNL,” which also featured musical guest KATSEYE.
During the monologue, Brunson opens up to audience questions. The camera pans to the crowd, revealing Brunson’s Knicks teammates Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Karl-Anthony Towns.
The crew asks some pretty unhinged questions. Bridges, for example, asks his buddy, “Are my arms, like, really long?”
And Anunoby, with his signature dry humor, asks Brunson about the ending of the NBA Finals’ Game 4 in which Anunoby famously tipped in Brunson’s failed 3-point attempt.
“Remember in Game Four when you took that shot in the end and you missed it?” Anunoby asks Brunson in front of the live studio audience.

Among the highlights of the Q&A sesh was Hart’s questions to Brunson. The pair, whose friendship stretches back to their years playing together in college at Villanova University, go back-and-forth, roasting one another.
“Is it true that you took $113 million pay cut just to re-sign with the Knicks?” Hart asks at one point, before following up. “So is that money like still up for grabs?”
Brunson also teases Hart about a failed layup.
“AI be looking so real!” Hart responds.
The four end up joining Brunson on stage at the end of the monologue in a picture-perfect moment for the starting five.

The group — who won the championship after a nail-biter on June 13, ending a 53-year-long championship drought — previously told TODAY that they owe much of their success to their undeniable chemistry. Their final game featured an epic comeback from being down 29 points, and Brunson explained that it was the crew’s faith in one another that allowed them to stay hopeful.

“I think what we found is that we built these past two years of us being together, we built a chemistry, we built a rapport where no matter what was going on in the game, we were going to find a way to turn it around and just kind of pick it up,” Brunson told hosts Savannah Guthrie and Craig Melvin.
“SNL” airs on NBC, a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of TODAY.com.

title: Ke Huy Quan Shares The Film That Introduced Him To His First Friendships
summary: Ke Huy Quan credits his early career as a Hollywood child star with introducing him to his first group of close friends.
story: Ke Huy Quan credits his early career as a Hollywood child star with introducing him to his first group of close friends.

The Chinese American actor, along with his parents and eight siblings, fled his home in Saigon for a Hong Kong refugee camp in 1978 after the end of Vietnam War. When he was 8, he and his family immigrated to Los Angeles, where he launched his Hollywood career as a child actor.

On the Sept. 27 edition of Sunday Sitdown, Quan recalled to TODAY’s Willie Geist how he landed the role of Short Round, Harrison Ford’s sidekick, in the 1984 blockbuster “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom.”
During his audition for the movie, Quan, who grew up speaking Cantonese, said he improvised when his English failed him.
“I remember saying like, ‘You cheat, Dr. Jones. You cheat!’ And (Ford) says, ‘Can you prove that I cheated?’ And then the more he challenged me, the more I ran out of words,” Quan recalled, laughing.
“I didn’t have any English words left to challenge him, so the only thing I did was I challenged him right back but in Cantonese,” he added.
It was Quan’s next movie, the 1985 kids adventure “The Goonies,” that changed his social life, he said.

The movie, which co-starred Martha Plimpton, Sean Astin, Corey Feldman, Kerri Green, Josh Brolin and Jeff Cohen, followed a close-knit group of friends who discover a treasure map and set out to find the fabled fortune of a pirate named One-Eyed Willy.
“I never had friends growing up because I come from such a big family,” said Quan, who recalled bonding with his young co-stars.
“We had such an amazing time together, and they didn’t treat me like an outsider. They treated me like I was one of their own,” Quan added.
The movie made such an impact, Quan borrowed from its “Goonies never say die” catchphrase for the title of his 2026 memoir, “Never Say Die.”
Quan starred in a few more projects as a young adult, including a role on the ABC sitcom “Head of the Class,” before the industry offers dried up.
“At that time, I didn’t understand it. I thought I would have an incredible career. I mean, I just came off of two big movies,” Quan said.
“I remember being really depressed, being, you know, dejected,” he added.
For the new two decades, Quan busied himself studying film at the University of Southern California and working behind the scenes on movies.
In 2022, he played Waymond Wang, a laundromat owner who battles the IRS, in the comedy-drama “Everything Everywhere All at Once.”
He won an Academy Award for the role.
For Quan, he said his career arc is a metaphor for the American Dream, the story of someone who is “given an opportunity to try, to fail, to get back up and try again.”

“When you think about my story, how improbable that was — how can this guy, who, yes, experienced some success when he was 12 years old and then disappeared for decades, how can he possibly come back with this little movie and win an Oscar?” he said.

“I look back in my early years, late teens, early 20s when I was struggling, when I was desperately wanting an opportunity,” he added. “Now having the benefit of hindsight, I wouldn’t change a thing. I’m so grateful for everything that has happened.”

title: Khloé Kardashian Is Ready to Find Her ‘Forever Person’ and Grow Her Family
summary: Khloé Kardashian tells TODAY.com she is open to dating, expanding her family and shares the biggest lesson age has taught her.
story: For almost two decades, Khloé Kardashian has let viewers witness some of the most intimate and joyous moments of her life.

The entrepreneur and reality star was only 23 years old when the first season of “Keeping Up With the Kardashians” premiered in 2007. The show ended in 2021 after 20 seasons, but she and her famous family continue to document their lives on “The Kardashians.”
Now, at the age of 42, Kardashian is looking for her “forever person,” would love to expand her family and knows that age and time gives you the best lessons in life.
Among the most important one she’s learned is being present and in the moment, “That’s probably my biggest one,” Kardashian tells TODAY.com.
Another major lesson that came with age is believing in herself and giving the same supportive energy to her needs as she gives to others.

“It’s so funny how when you’re young and everyone’s like, ‘Oh, the older you get you really just don’t care what people think.’ And I’m not saying I don’t care what anyone thinks, I do. But the pool is getting smaller of people that I care about what they think of me,” she explains.
For example, starting her “Khloé in Wonder Land” podcast in 2025 was a major risk she took after struggling with self confidence in her mid-30s.

Kardashian says she used to feel “so confident, so secure” prior to that time in her life. “I would try any new business venture. If it failed, I was like, ‘Who cares? Everyone fails at things. Great learning lesson. Let’s move on.’”

“Then I got to a point I wouldn’t try anything because I got so in my head. Just, ‘Failure is bad, and everyone’s going to look at me a certain way.’ And I just felt so judged by so many people. I really let that get to me,” she recalls. “I would be rooting for everyone else and say such positive things to everyone. And then finally, I was like, ‘Why don’t I give myself the same energy I’m giving everybody else?’”
So what changed? Going to therapy, she says, changed her perspective.

“I’m like, ‘OK, what if it doesn’t do well? What does that mean?’ That means, ‘OK, it didn’t do well. Let’s pivot, do something else,’ and that does come with age,” she says. “That came with also working on myself. But a lot of it was like, you know what? Who cares? I’m growing up. I want to be more secure with myself. I want to show my kids that you should try new things.”
Since entering her 40s, Kardashian says she feels “really free and good within myself.”
“I feel really powerful, and I missed that because I had that for so many years and for about a decade, maybe a little less, I really lost that,” she says, “I’m proud that I was able to get it back.”
That confidence has translated to more business ventures, comfortable in her own skin and ready to put herself out in the dating world.
Season 8 of “The Kardashians” premieres Oct. 8. The trailer released mid-September teases Kardashian saying she’s single, ready to mingle and wanting more children.
“Oh my gosh, my daughter (True) asked me today about more kids, about a sister. I’m like, Oh my gosh!,” she says, adding that her children are “begging for it.”
“I’m like, I don’t know what I’m going to do. But I love kids, so I definitely need to figure out my life.”
Life is busy for Kardashian, who says she’s “definitely single” but open to meeting someone special.
“I want to put myself out there. I do want to find a forever person. I also want to just date and not have pressure on that,” she explains, adding that she just wants to have fun.
“That’s what I want first to ease myself into it. I just don’t even know how you do that in today’s day and age,” Kardashian says with a laugh. “I need help. It’s tough, right?”

Kardashian was previously married to Lamar Odom and shares daughter True, 8, and son Tatum, 4, with ex-boyfriend Tristan Thompson. Over the years she’s expressed that she’s not looking to date ... until now.
“I don’t know how to help myself, so I think that’s my biggest challenge,” she says. “But anyone reading this, I’ll take tips and advice.”

title: Backstreet Boys Re-Create Iconic ‘Millennium Tour’ Surfboard Entrance— And Fans Are Not OK
summary: The Backstreet Boys re-created their “Into the Millennium” entrance, riding futuristic surfboards as they opened their first show for their German residency.
story: Check on your friends who are Backstreet Boys fans, they might be unwell.
The group kicked off their “Into The Millennium HOMECOMING: Live in Germany” shows on Friday, Sept. 25 and made an unforgettable entrance that is making fans nostalgic.

In video shared on their Instagram, dramatic music plays as the five singers — Kevin Richardson, AJ McLean, Nick Carter, Howie Dorough and Brian Littrell  — are dressed in black-and-blue ensembles and ascending from the sky on surfboards.
“…but were you ready??” they captioned the video.
After seeing the video of their surfboard entrances fans freaked out online.
“LOSING MY FREAKING MIND I CANNOT HANDLE THIS GET ME TO GERMANY NOOOOOOW!!!!! I am shaking typing this!!!!!!THE SURFBOARDS!!!!! I’m NAUSEOUS!!!! OMGGGG,” one person wrote.
“Oh d---, are you serious? 😱😱😱😱 No, I wasn’t prepared for this. That’s so awesome—you guys are just amazing,” another added.
“Omg I would have DIED,” “Screaming crying throwing up!” and “I. CANT. BREATHE” are among other strong reactions from fans.

Longtime BSB fans recall this epic entrance from their 1999 “Into the Millennium Tour.” Back then, they flew in on futuristic surfboards also while wearing coordinated looks that consisted of royal blue strapped vests, checkered long sleeves and navy pants.
As they made their way to the stage, they opened with “Larger Than Life.”

“There was a couple of flubs that happened on the ‘Millennium’ tour when we used to fly up to the crowd. Kevin got stuck up there one night,” McLean told TODAY.com in 2025 when first announcing their Sphere residency shows in Las Vegas.
Richardson added that he “got stuck up there for, like, three songs.”
This time around, all appeared to go well during the 2026 rendition of the memorable opening.
The Backstreet Boys are performing a number of shows during their first German residency at Merkur Spiel-Arena Düsseldorf.
They previously shared that the location is special as it’s the first country “that ever embraced the Backstreet Boys.”
“You saw who we were before the rest of the world even knew we existed. For this, we are forever grateful, and after 30 years, we are finally coming home,” they wrote on social media.
These concerts come after their highly successful “Into the Millennium” Sphere residency in Las Vegas that was announced on TODAY in February of 2025.
The show is a nod to their 1999 third studio album, “Millennium,” that includes hits “I Want It That Way,” “Larger Than Life” and “Show Me the Meaning of Being Lonely.”
What was meant to be a series of summer shows in 2025 has since continued, with more Sphere shows expected at the end of this year.

title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Babylon,’ Explained by 2 History Professors
summary: Taylor Swift’s new song “Babylon” is about a failed relationship and references a famous city of Mesopotamia. Here’s what to know.
story: Taylor Swift’s new song “Babylon” brings a big historical symbol to describe the arc of one relationship that ends before a person realizes how good it was.
It’s part of four new songs Swift dropped as part of her “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” album on Sept. 25.

“Babylon” is told in the second person, with Swift singing to directly to “you.” That “you” is described as a man who left home — a “small town,” to be specific. He’s said to be an ambitious “libertine” who later “longs for home.”

When he meets a girl who loves him, it “stopped you cold.” He kept her at arm’s length, though, and kept things “never official.” But in a flash forward during the bridge, Swift sings that “you” seemingly went on to start a family, but he misses the most important parts. She sings about a vignette of a woman hanging Christmas lights with the subject of the song’s son and later calling her mom to say, “It’s not working/ It’s just not worth it if we’re not what he wants.”
That all culminates in an explanation of the song’s chorus, which describes the subject on a train with his “headphones gone,” realizing the song he thought he hated, he actually loves.
“Then that melody is all you want/ You never knew that it was Babylon/ ‘Til it was gone,” Swift sings.

Taken alone, the song implies that Babylon is an idyllic setting, set in the past and something to perpetually long for. But the reference has a storied history. The city is referenced in more than a few pop songs, including a 1998 hit by David Gray and a 2020 song by Lady Gaga.

Wait, What is Babylon?
Babylon was an ancient city located in the middle of what is now Iraq, between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

Amanda Podany, a professsor emeritus of history at California State Polytechnic University, tells TODAY.com Babylon is associated with the idea of ruin. Alexander the Great, as legend has it, razed the city, though Podany says that might not have been the case. Still, the legend persisted.

“There’s plenty of evidence for Babylon continuing to be an important place for hundreds of years after that. But again, that sort of went into the popular consciousness as a metaphor for ruin, as a metaphor for something glorious that that fell,” she says.
Its place in pop culture was potentially solidified in the Bible.

“In the Bible, Babylon gets really bad press,” Lloyd Llewellyn-Jones, professor at the University of Cardiff, tells TODAY.com. “It is the ultimate City of Sin; Babylon is the Mother of Harlots; it is home to the Whore of Babylon, whose reign will usher in Armageddon and bring about the Apocalypse.”
But he says the city was actually one of the most sophisticated in the ancient world.

“It was the first ever metropolis, with an enormous multi-cultural population. It was the centre of arts, literature, culture, and industry. It was New York, Paris, Bangkok, Los Angeles and London rolled into one. There was no city on earth to rival it. Babylon was the Mother of All Cities,” he says.
But Podany doesn’t think the Babylon in this song is associated with sinfulness or ruin.

“She seems to be using it as a stand-in for that place that you didn’t realize was the best until you left it or lost it. So she’s choosing, I think, to not view Babylon as representing its kings (some of whom were, yes, imperialistic and brutal), or its supposed wickedness; she’s looking past all the layers of misunderstanding that have accumulated on the word Babylon,” she said.

In a twist Podany called interesting (and perhaps not intentional), she’s associating Babylon with nostalgia, “in the way ancient Babylonians would have indeed felt about the place 3,000 or 4,000 years ago, perhaps when they were traveling far away.”
She continued, “Babylon would have been remembered as a beloved home.”
